texto: We did a spin-off, and I ended up with Portrait of a Lady on Fire. I went into this movie completely blind. I didn't know anything about it. The first thing that caught me was how visually appealing it is. Cinematically, I can absolutely see why people praise this movie so much. The cinematography, the framing, the performances, and the overall presentation are beautiful. The story is about two women and the relationship that develops between them. I understood what the movie was trying to say, and I could see the depth of their connection. I've also seen people call this one of the most perfect romances ever made, and some even compared its emotional impact to Titanic. But honestly, it didn't hit me that way. For me, I was watching it as a movie rather than emotionally placing myself inside the relationship. Even during the final moments, when people say the movie becomes extremely emotional, I was honestly just thinking, "How long is this going to take?" That doesn't mean I think the movie is bad. Quite the opposite. I think it's an excellent film from a cinematic perspective, and I'm glad I explored something completely different. I believe this is also my first French movie. But emotionally, it just wasn't for me. Maybe I'm simply not someone who connects strongly with romantic stories, and I've never personally experienced being in love, so perhaps that's one reason I couldn't connect with the relationship on that deeper level. 3.5/5

texto: Another one for psych class. This is one of the worst films I've ever seen. The performances are mediocre, with DiCaprio's likely being the worst. The writing is incredibly juvenile, even with the plausible theory that the majority of the dialogue is filtered through the guy's warped mind. The film doesn't even look good or have an interesting aesthetic. The twist falls apart because it requires you to empathize with DiCaprio's character in the beginning, which I did not. Now, to the big problems. This film's portrayal of the mentally ill is disgusting. I understand that the facility is specifically meant to house people who've committed a violent crime, but the film was arguably still irresponsible in its perpetuation of the stereotype that all people with mental illness are scary, violent, completely irrational, and are deserving of no empathy whatsoever. There is no mention of the specific diagnosis that any patient, let alone the main character, has, which makes it impossible to understand the accuracy of the portrayals. This film was made too recently to still exhibit such an under-researched and outdated parody of what a real group of underprivileged people is like. Let's move on to another problem, the film's portrayal of both the Holocaust and the implications of Project MKUltra during the Cold War. These were both serious tragedies that I feel were not handled with appropriate sensitivity and were rather just half-baked elements seemingly thrown in for added novelty. With this film exhibiting these two themes in addition to its portrayal of extreme psychosis, there are too many things being explored and none of them are done properly. The main conspiracy is clearly supposed to be MKUltra, something that really did victimize psychiatric patients during the Cold War, and yet in the movie's cannon, it's confirmed to not be happening. I don't think this film is intentionally trying to say that MKUltra didn't happen, but it's a very strange and poorly thought-out choice that is completely at odds with the setting. This movie clearly did not have anything to say about any of the incredibly serious topics it includes, and thus has no comprehensive or unique thesis. It's an offensive, confused mess that frankly has no merit as a piece of art.

texto: Le film se laisse agréablement suivre mais une fois la promenade terminée le point de vue où on arrive est décevant. Parce que c'est le même paysage qu'on voit depuis le début. Les ficelles qui sous-tendent l'ensemble sont trop visibles. En plus d'être visibles, elles sont trop serrées, elles contraignent la lecture d'un film qui a pourtant conscience de la force de l'ambiguïté émotionnelle qu'il pourrait produire chez le spectateur. La première mixture de réel et d'hallucination après un moment d'homogénéité apparente et intrigante finit par se soumettre aux lois physiques et se décante jusqu'à exposer clairement chacun de ses composants. La seconde mixture de monstruosité et d'humanité est juste insipide. Le crime qui est présenté n'est pas le crime d'un fou par perversion mais celui d'un fou de douleur. Le film justifie sa violence après avoir fait défendre la thèse d'une violence intraseque à l'humanité a l'un de ses personnages. Sauf qu'on ne le voit pas et l'ensemble échou à jeter le trouble dans lequel le regard de la femme qui pose son doigt sur sa bouche promettait de nous plonger.

texto: entretenida pelicula e interesante final, pero todo el aspecto “psicológico” de la pelicula lo senti muy cliche que me arruino el resto. muy fantástico para sentirlo real. sobretodo de personajes que deberian aterrizar los conceptos psicológicos. solo hacen que la pelicula se sienta mas como un “esto es lo que creemos que las condiciones psicológicas son en hollywood”. me saca de la inmersion y no pude evitar reirme. 5 estrellas si tuviera 14-16 años. muy dramatizado y caracterizado hasta sentirse holllywoodense, pero puede hacerse un espacio a la discusión teniendo en cuenta el cine noir, la pelicula no falla en hacer homenaje a los thrillers característicos de la epoca de estos, pero si senti que era muy “en tu cara”. no que no sea una peli entrete de ver. english: Entertaining movie with an interesting ending, but the entire “psychological” aspect of the film felt very cliché to me, and it ruined the rest. It was too fantastical to feel realistic, especially coming from characters who are supposed to ground these psychological concepts. Very dramatized and characterized to the point of feeling overly Hollywood-like, but it can still have a place for discussion when considering film noir. texto: "You have to let her go" "I can't!" "Then you'll never get off this island..." Enjoyed this more on rewatch, I was better able to appreciate how the mood of the island is developed, with the soundscape being particularly impressive, with original score, licensed music, and classical music all coming together really well. Weather is also used particularly effectively to make the island feel isolating and uncomfortable; there's something about heavy rain at night that makes me really uncomfortable and I love the way that is used in this film. The star segment here is Ward C, feeling like walking into a nightmare within an already dreadful environment - it feels like those segments in Silent Hill when you go from normal world to Otherworld, everything just gets so suddenly worse and terrifying with no end in sight. Despite this being a psychological thriller with heavy emphasis on its ending, it still does very little for me compared to the build up on the island (which I really enjoyed) and other films in the ending-heavy "genre" (Memento, Prestige, Fight Club, Total Recall, etc.). It just never feels like the reveals that happen meaningfully impact or re-contextualize the earlier scenes of the film. Of course the context does literally change but it doesn't really change the emotional impacts, at least for me

texto: I personally think it is a psychedelic paranoid masterpiece that is a wonderful examination of the brain, trauma, and crisis of identity. All themes which Scorsese has used before for his movies. The film is creepy, beautifully shot, extremely well acted, and leaves you in suspense until the end. While it may not break new ground the way Taxi Driver, Mean Streets, and Goodfellas do, it is one of the most beautifully shot films I’ve ever seen, and I find it quite emotionally impactful. So why do you think Shutter Island hasn’t aged as well as his other works? Even Scorsese himself said he regrets being attached to it, and I think that’s wrong because it shows just how versatile the guy is. He can direct any genre to perfection.

texto: 50 Across the Spider-Verse is a film that promises everything and delivers... some of it. The multiverse concept, inherently thrilling on paper, remains the franchise's greatest asset. The sheer variety of Spider-People is a joy to behold. The film does not disappoint in its ambition. Yet for all its formal brilliance, Across the Spider-Verse stumbles badly in its handling of tone, and nowhere is this more evident than in its villain. His early appearances are played purely for laughs, and while the film eventually attempts to pivot toward genuine menace, the damage is already done. He becomes a symbol of the film's broader comedic excess: the relentless quipping and meta-references that undercut every moment of tension. By the time The Spot transforms into a world-ending threat, we cannot take him seriously because the film never taught us how. The film's incessant needle drops compound the problem, each licensed track feeling less like organic storytelling and more like a calculated monetization strategy. The soundtrack is curated not to serve the narrative but to populate Spotify playlists, a transparent effort to generate revenue streams beyond the box office. This commercial calculation extends beyond the music. The cliffhanger ending? It is difficult not to view it as a deliberate fragmentation, a way to stretch a single story across multiple releases and maximize returns. What emerges is not a complete story but a dazzlingly packaged installment, one that too often feels engineered for the franchise rather than the narrative. 🕷️Homecoming Review🕷️ 🕸️Far From Home Review🕸️ 🦇The Dark Knight Review🦇 🕷️No Way Home Review🕷️ 🕸️Spider-Man Review🕸️ 🕷️Spider-Man 2 Review🕷️ 🕸️Into the Spider-Verse Review🕸️

texto: Really wanted to like this one more than I did. After all, what better way to complete my Trolls Remorse arc than giving a favorable score to the Other Miles Morales movie. Sadly, this is a textbook case of chief creatives whose eyes are far, far bigger than their stomachs. The worst of the post Gunn, post Waititi “Comic Book Authenticity” is depicted here, and this time I truly do not believe that any of the 3 writers have any kind of fondness for the comics. The focus of Across the Spider-Verse is selling moviegoers on the importance of Spider-Man as a brand within Marvel, with a set of rules to be followed; a checklist of inciting traumas to be applied where the end result is a new Spider-Man. Conveniently, the film makes this subtext text by centering the film around the prevention of “Canon Events”, tragic deaths of loved ones that must happen because That’s Spider-Man. Mercifully, Lord and Miller rarely show our massive cast experience or be changed by said traumas — a film that thinks for itself, what a Marvel. Having read more comics than I think 99% of Letterboxd, Alternate Universe stories are among some of the laziest writing one can choose. The superior first film largely uses it for Family Guy cutaway tier gags; “Hey remember the Spider-Man Popsicle” novelty signaling to the adults in the room that this is Growing the Brand but fun. Now we must succumb to the Elseworlds Comic Story Effect: writing essentially a re-themed take on the platonic Spider Man second outing, each moment signposted through overt “meta” staging, and a complete wet fart of a 15 minute 3rd act after a 70 minute 1st to boot. One would hope that character could carry us through a lackluster script, but Lord and Miller and The Other One opt for a thin but wide approach instead. It feels as if character attributes were chosen at complete random. Jessica Drew is a strong black woman working while pregnant because… Ben Reilly is brooding because the 90s were grim and dark (yet nothing in the handful of Ben Reilly appearances I’ve read would even touch the vicinity of brooding). Like the aforementioned Cutaway Gags, characters who could be Sneakers O’Toolesian delightful non sequiturs overstay their welcome and confuse. The hired gun Lego commercial got an earnest laugh out of me, everything in the set pieces to follow would not. Once again the thankless job of creating something worth writing paragraphs about falls to the Animators. Eyes and stomachs in perfect alignment, they truly deliver on great leaps forward in mainstream animation. No minced words about it: this film can look gorgeous . However, due to the complete dearth of imagination from the top down everything feels off. I found myself getting genuinely overstimulated by the film at times; nothing moves right, scenes feel poorly timed, and not a single moment felt as effortlessly evocative as the sequence in the first film where Miles leaps off a building into a colorful void. Around the 50 minute mark, as we wind down on the prologue, Across starts to look legitimately ugly. Chromatic blurs fill the screen for no other reason than to exist, the camera rapidly adjusts itself throughout a scene, and your eyes struggle to find a place to rest while taking in the composition. Very few of the colorful compositions have meaning, I struggle to ascribe any real meaning to heavy decisions like a Trans Reading for Gwen because of how arbitrary the movie can look; the curtains are simply blue. It is creative flailing, masquerading as vision. People with little experience in either often call comics and film sister mediums. Both deal in the marriage of language and visual, and storyboarding kinda feels like a comic to the layman. The analogy can be allowed to continue to live regarding Across the Spider-Verse because the disconnect between animator and Director/Writer/Producer feels as if they couldn’t be any further apart — as if the worst instincts of American comics is a style to be worshipped and imitated. If you’ve ever read a bad comic with good art you’ll understand what I mean. If you haven’t, you can buy Kingdom Come for like 10 bucks now.

texto: 50 Across the Spider-Verse is a film that promises everything and delivers... some of it. The multiverse concept, inherently thrilling on paper, remains the franchise's greatest asset. The sheer variety of Spider-People is a joy to behold. The film does not disappoint in its ambition. Yet for all its formal brilliance, Across the Spider-Verse stumbles badly in its handling of tone, and nowhere is this more evident than in its villain. His early appearances are played purely for laughs, and while the film eventually attempts to pivot toward genuine menace, the damage is already done. He becomes a symbol of the film's broader comedic excess: the relentless quipping and meta-references that undercut every moment of tension. By the time The Spot transforms into a world-ending threat, we cannot take him seriously because the film never taught us how. The film's incessant needle drops compound the problem, each licensed track feeling less like organic storytelling and more like a calculated monetization strategy. The soundtrack is curated not to serve the narrative but to populate Spotify playlists, a transparent effort to generate revenue streams beyond the box office. This commercial calculation extends beyond the music. The cliffhanger ending? It is difficult not to view it as a deliberate fragmentation, a way to stretch a single story across multiple releases and maximize returns. What emerges is not a complete story but a dazzlingly packaged installment, one that too often feels engineered for the franchise rather than the narrative. 🕷️Homecoming Review🕷️ 🕸️Far From Home Review🕸️ 🦇The Dark Knight Review🦇 🕷️No Way Home Review🕷️ 🕸️Spider-Man Review🕸️ 🕷️Spider-Man 2 Review🕷️ 🕸️Into the Spider-Verse Review🕸️

texto: Au moins aussi acclamé à sa sortie, ce second opus a le mérite d'être divertissant, mais à l'inverse du premier qui était une montée en puissance sur tous les plans, plus les enjeux multiversels prennent du poids, et moins il convainc. Spider-Man : Across the Spider-Verse est bien meilleur lorsqu'il se concentre sur l'intime, même s'il demeure à ce sujet très classique. D'ailleurs, j'ai bien cru que je le préférerais à en juger par son introduction, plus aboutie que celle du précédent, mais la suite m'a déçu. Il est très frustrant de regarder une œuvre qui s'étend sur autant de temps pour ne pas avoir le droit à une vraie fin, fut-elle ouverte. Sur le plan visuel, on est dans la continuité, avec un peu plus de variété issue de l'exploration du multivers. Toutefois, je regrette l'inclusion de live action qui me sort totalement du film. Ponctuellement, certains plans continuent de me gêner par leur façon de trancher avec d'autres mais je dois dire que cela a moins été le cas qu'auparavant. C'est peut-être une question d'habitude, mais je pense surtout que celui-ci est techniquement plus abouti. Quoi que je sois critique, cela reste à des années lumières des bouses super-heroïques que nous sert Marvel à son habitude. Le moment est plaisant mais hormis toute la séquence où Gwen et Miles se retrouvent puis papotent en se collant sur les bâtiments — qui est superbe — je ne sais pas si j'en retiendrais grand chose sur le long terme. En fait, je me rends bien compte que toutes mes scènes préférées sont dans le premier acte. Après, comme c'est une expérience formelle, je suppose qu'il a l'avantage de bien se revoir. La sortie de la suite sera l'occassion de le réévaluer.

texto: Man, I really wanted to like this movie more, I loved the first movie. And make no mistake, the first two thirds of this sequel were everything I'd hoped for, gorgeous animation and art style as expected, an interesting plot with a hilarious villain who unexpectedly goes through development into a more dangerous, malevolent foe. And the sheer amount of non-intrusive cameos when they arrive at Spider City, and Oscar Isaac's performance! But with the third act everything just... falls apart. All sense of momentum stops dead in its tracks. The bad guy fails to fulfill the menace and character growth he'd promised, because the movie never actually gets that far. What should be an exciting climax instead wastes time with useless drama and a misdirection that doesn't actually add anything to plot or character, but rather just bloats out the runtime to a level Eternals would have been proud of. And then.... "To Be Continued...... in Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse!" Uh.... okay. Sure. Cut out the third act of a film, the most important part of any movie where all the tension and drama pays off, and then relegate to a sequel which will likely not arrive for years to come. And instead of an alternate climax, just fill out the last 40 minutes with mind-numbingly boring and unsatisfactory screentime. Man, what a disappointment.

texto: I think this film is really great, but I think with it being a Part 1 - and with the whole story being about Miles' trying to prove he's allowed to exist - it falls slightly short to other Spiderman films. The story is constantly leading up to something bigger and better, but we never see it. Worldbuilding-wise, this film is definitely strong; but it requires the sequel or prequel to feel fleshed out - it's not great as a standalone. On the other hand, Spot is a sick villain and I think using him as a mechanism to talk about the Spiderverse collapsing is amazing.

texto: I do not envy anyone given the task of following Into the Spider-Verse. That film singularly injected so much new life and artistic innovation into an IP that was beginning to get stagnant. It took the time and consideration to acknowledge the foundation and rich history baked into the character of Spider-Man and gave it a loving sendoff before turning to a brand new chapter. Regrettably, Across the Spider-Verse feels like one step forward, two steps back. If there’s one thing my journey through the MCU has taught me, it’s that the multiverse fucking sucks. And I understand that’s a contentious position to hold against a series called “the Spider-Verse,” but hear me out. Into the Spider-Verse used the concept in the most effective way: minimalistic. The multiverse purely acted as the inciting incident for Miles’ story, much like time travel in the first Terminator movie. Yes, you had cheeky references to established Spider-Man iterations, their tropes and standing in pop culture, but ultimately it was a measuring stick to hold up to Miles’ own hero’s journey. A narrative device showing how the character inspired this new hero, much like he has countless others in our own world. Comparatively, Across the Spider-Verse becomes overindulgent, languishing in its multiverse setting and using it as an excuse to showcase the less popular Spider-Man content, or ride the coattails of the more popular content. Remember Andrew Garfield Spider-Man? Look, there he is! And Toby McGuire! Look, this multiversal Spider-Man agency knows about what Dr. Strange was doing! And the dimension-hopping films? He talks to Mrs. Chen, from our hit Venom film series! The SPUM-C is alive and well. And look, there’s Donald Glover as Prowler! Like he was gonna be in the MCU! There’s also an attempt to make each dimension extremely unique, which unfortunately comes across like a more obnoxious attempt to copy the uniqueness of Into the Spider-Verse’s art style, and the clashing artstyles tend to make it look like a big, muddled mess. Really, with a concept like the multiverse, the last thing you want to do is get technical. Where Deadpool & Wolverine had the braindead concept of an anchor being, Across the Spider-Verse presents the “canon events.” (Which felt like such a dumb attempt at meta, I threw up in my mouth a little bit.) Rather than the shared trauma being a bonding point between the different iterations of Spider-Man, it’s now an absolute event necessary for their journey, whose disruption could lead to the disintegration of their reality. Delving more into the multiverse also takes the wind out of the sails for Miles’ own character arc. Spoilers: we find out that he wasn’t meant to become Spider-Man, as the spider that bit him came from another dimension. So he is an anomaly, and his arc is that, even though it wasn’t his destiny…he is still Spider-Man. Because he chooses to be. Which isn’t nothing , but feels like a much more hollow echo of his arc in the first film. My own cynicism and hangups notwithstanding, Across the Spider-Verse is a fine film. A far fall from its predecessor, but if you’ve been missing the characters and world, it does feel like a welcome return. It’s overbloated, and its standing as a definitive “part one” further lessens its value on its own, but it’s ultimately competent enough.

texto: Man, I really wanted to like this movie more, I loved the first movie. And make no mistake, the first two thirds of this sequel were everything I'd hoped for, gorgeous animation and art style as expected, an interesting plot with a hilarious villain who unexpectedly goes through development into a more dangerous, malevolent foe. And the sheer amount of non-intrusive cameos when they arrive at Spider City, and Oscar Isaac's performance! But with the third act everything just... falls apart. All sense of momentum stops dead in its tracks. The bad guy fails to fulfill the menace and character growth he'd promised, because the movie never actually gets that far. What should be an exciting climax instead wastes time with useless drama and a misdirection that doesn't actually add anything to plot or character, but rather just bloats out the runtime to a level Eternals would have been proud of. And then.... "To Be Continued...... in Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse!" Uh.... okay. Sure. Cut out the third act of a film, the most important part of any movie where all the tension and drama pays off, and then relegate to a sequel which will likely not arrive for years to come. And instead of an alternate climax, just fill out the last 40 minutes with mind-numbingly boring and unsatisfactory screentime. Man, what a disappointment.

That degree of difficulty is furthered when the eldest child is borderline revolutionary — as seen with the latest two animated Spider-Man feature films, Into the Spider-Verse and Across the Spider-Verse. texto: I think this film is really great, but I think with it being a Part 1 - and with the whole story being about Miles' trying to prove he's allowed to exist - it falls slightly short to other Spiderman films. The story is constantly leading up to something bigger and better, but we never see it. Worldbuilding-wise, this film is definitely strong; but it requires the sequel or prequel to feel fleshed out - it's not great as a standalone. On the other hand, Spot is a sick villain and I think using him as a mechanism to talk about the Spiderverse collapsing is amazing.

texto: Não sou tão chegado nesse quanto no primeiro. Não que ele peque no início; pelo contrário, é até empolgante ter as boas-vindas a esse universo novamente. O único incômodo que sinto é essa forma meio frenética da história, acelerada demais e com excesso de diálogos e comentários jogados com comédia excessiva. Mas acredito que, do meio para os finalmentes, é onde ele realmente compensa. Essa parte do Miles driblando mais de 100 cabeças de teia é coisa que a gente pede para ver sem nem saber: uma adaptação da genialidade do Aranha em combate. Trilha sonora, tensão crescente e diálogos com tom de mistério nesse desfecho praticamente fazem da melhor cena do filme.

texto: If Into the Spider-Verse felt like a comic book flipped at 24 frames per second, significant stretches of this one felt like it was flipped at 48. The animation is absolutely breathtaking, and the juggling act of all these characters, dimensions, and styles is remarkable, but the film’s constant need to stimulate becomes overstimulating: there’s always music, movement, and something happening in the background, rarely giving you room to breathe. The "Achilles' heel" of the multiverse concept is partly that there’s simply too much going on, and this movie occasionally falls into its own trap. The best parts are when it slows down. The Spot is introduced in an interesting way, but never really gets the one-on-one dynamic with Spider-Man you want from a central villain, partly because the emotional anchor is spread across so many characters that there’s nowhere obvious to attach yourself. It’s a double-edged sword: the concept is strong and the execution is often remarkable, but the emotional center is spread too thin. Still, the set pieces and animation are incredible, and the new dimensions it opens up are exciting. The ending leaves plenty on the table for the next chapter, and I’m excited to see where it goes. It’s still a very good animated film, but I prefer the first one, which somehow managed to balance all of this perfectly.

texto: Almost a 5 star flick. “Nah, ima do my own thing” don’t even get me started on this movie because I could probably go on forever. Spider-Man Across the Spider-Verse was actually so good. The animation is probably one of the coolest things I’ve ever seen in a movie, and every scene looks like it could be a piece of art. The action was crazy, the characters were really fun, and Miles’ story got way more serious this time. I also really liked seeing all the different Spider-People and how unique each one was. The whole movie just had so much energy and never felt boring. I didn’t really like spit in this movie, I think that’s what brought it down for me, I’d give it 4.5/5 stars because there were a couple things I didn’t love, especially the ending because it leaves you with a huge cliffhanger. But besides that, this movie was amazing and definitely lived up to the hype. Miles is such a great Spider-Man, and the movie made me even more excited to see what happens next. Definitely one of my favorite Spider-Man movies. Can’t wait for beyond the spiderverse. Please watch it

texto: This film was a no-fun labor to watch. Only gave it 2 stars for the performances by some of the actors. First, the narrative is all over the place. It's not anti-war, it's not pro-freedom fighters, it's just ambiguous. Shot like documentary and news footage half of the time, and it still seems like an exaggerated narrative, towards what goal? Not sure really. Both sides kill civilians because of reasons. Everyone sucks. But if the whole "war=bad" narrative was the goal, Paths of Glory did it much better 9 years earlier. None of the characters were likeable, none had enough development to really understand or even care about. All were cold emotionally and dehumanized. Even if you were looking for a "fair" way to describe both sides being bad, this movie did a poor job of it. Film quality was terrible, cinematography wasn't great, even for its era. 2001 came just 2 years after this and looked like it's from another century. I watched better, lower budget documentary films from modern wars like the Syrian Civil War or the Afghanistan War that were far more compelling and up to date with modern filming quality. I just don't get the hype. This genuinely was a bore and a chore to watch.

exemplo: Críticas apontam que o filme parece ter um viés político, com uma abordagem que pode ser interpretada como propaganda, e que não equilibra as perspectivas de ambas as partes envolvidas.
texto: While often enshrined as a cinematic masterpiece, The Battle of Algiers reveals itself upon closer inspection to be a technically flawed work of state-sponsored propaganda that priorities political utility over artistic integrity. It is profoundly shallow in character observation and attempts to substitute the hollowness of the narrative with the heaviness of the topic (colonialism). As this film was commissioned by the Algerian government and produced by an FLN commander, the impact of other Algerian resistance movements are completely ignored and instead the film is to function as a seemingly authentic origin story propaganda. The film’s celebrated documentary aesthetic is revolutionary, but is undercut by multiple weak formal aspects. The lighting in particular is jarringly inconsistent, often featuring blindingly bright front-lighting in scenes where no logical light source exists. Even between cuts of the same scene, the front-lighting persists into the new perspective, resulting in continuity errors and shifting shadows that shatter the very immersion the film claims to cultivate. This is compounded by an uneven sound design that lack consistency in dynamic and integration. Furthermore, mechanical cuts stitch scenes together without transition or narrative juxtaposition. As a result, the film feel like a collection of in-cohesive fragments that lacks vision. As mentioned previously, the film disguises narrative depth by the weight of its topic rather than by the quality of its writing. Despite the film's attempt to imitate observational realism, characters are treated as hollow ideological devices rather than real humans beings. The much applauded non-professional actor, Brahim Hadjadj, performs an Ali la Pointe that is painfully one-dimensional and mechanical, providing no window into the character's psyche (to the point that it is difficult to even recognise him as the protagonist). Ironically, the "villainous" Colonel Mathieu is given more complexity and range, feeling slightly more like a real individual instead of just a hollow political vessel. The film’s most egregious flaw is its poorly executed mechanical emotional manipulation from its sound and visual language. Death and suffering of Algerians are accompanied with religious scores and manufactured tears to evoke sanctity and martyrdom. In contrast, the death of European innocents are treated with cold, percussive score and lack of emotional outburst (even from themselves) to trivialise the tragedy. Disregarding the intent, the ostentatious and un-serious execution results in theatricality that ends up losing emotional grounding. Ultimately, The Battle of Algiers is less a work of art and more a technical manual for insurgency. It fails the "show, don't tell" rule with its paradoxical, dry narration and expositions that explains the how of the conflict while speaking little on the historical why. Concerningly, the film also directly proclaims the effectiveness of terrorism as a mean to gain UN support as well as the potency of torture (despite many research indicate otherwise). In the film's final scene, the irony of shouting for independence in the language of the coloniser is perhaps the film's most profound and most honest observation about the lasting scars of imperialism, yet unsurprisingly this is a depth that clearly escapes the interest of the film.

texto: The premise described on letterboxed doesn’t start until nearly 50 minutes in. Prior to that, all we’re watching are radical extremists blowing up random civilians, which eventually comes together into some measure of purpose by the end. The sparse but thoughtful lines of dialogue illuminate the different narratives we use to try to justify our actions. The torture, tricks, and escalating tactics can be effective at times, but the film is ultimately at odds with itself. It wants to depict the mechanizations of revolution without sympathetic characters, only sympathetic factions. That’s admirable, but then it relies on excessive crash zooms and close ups on random crying people, a cheap, easy way to get the viewer enraged. Though I shouldn’t say random because they’re almost always the radicals, who by the end, are just terrorists gunning down pedestrian women. The film is not as impartial as it wants us to think it is, and unfortunately, I found myself kinda siding with the colonists who by and large followed some kind of ethical code (even if random grunts broke it on occasion). The radicals, by contrast, were so conniving that it really did feel like the colonists had every right to be suspicious of them. I think we’re naturally drawn to side with the underdogs because we know that their options are far more limiting, but I also think if they’d focused on actually targeting the French military, instead of regular people, or otherwise did anything that showed them rustling with the moral lows they were stooping to, it would have revealed their humanity in a way that shoving a camera into someone’s face doesn’t.

texto: Watching Black & White Movies #5 Twentieth-century evil for me is embodied in the terrorization of militaries operating brutally, efficiently, and without remorse. Yes, Mathieu embodies this threat. But don’t Ali La Pointe and Saadi Yacef Djafar as well? In that sense, the film is careful to show that history’s judgment depends on which side of it you occupy (eg. maybe French colonialism is bad and the french suck!) What the film captures exceptionally well is the terror created by war, portraying both sides in meticulous detail. The reason I rated it so low is that this documentary-style approach leaves Mathieu as the only substantially developed character. As a result, I find it difficult to see the film as a full exploration of its subject; it’s a documentary-esque sequence of events, but not a “complete” examination of the conflict. Its nuance is incomplete. Rather than offering a truly comprehensive portrayal, it presents a focused account that inevitably privileges certain perspectives over others. Italian neorealism is not particularly my thing either and this is a rare Morricone score miss. At the very least it is completely impossible to dislike the Mathieu discussing Sartre scene love you Sarte.

texto: Oh, good for them. I appreciate the efforts to recreate these events in a documentary/newsreel style, the ways it shows the horrors of taking up arms to reclaim one's country, & the clear political & human viewpoint behind it all. I'm sure it was especially groundbreaking when it was released, hence all the accolades. I respect it for what it is. I think I would've liked it more if they'd made it more like a feature though & focused on a few characters to make everything they go through hit harder. As horrific as some of this is, none of it lands emotionally for me. I feel removed from the whole thing. Plus, I've long understood that when humans turn to violence to solve a problem, it's always ugly & upsetting. Also, colonialism is bad, mmkay? Not news to me, though I'll admit I wasn't previously aware of these specific events. So at least I learned something tonight.

texto: La bataille d'Alger est un film incontournable sur la guerre d'Algérie, il est même le plus connu internationalement. Le film se déroule durant une période précise de la guerre que l'on appelle « la bataille d'Alger », période qui a duré de 1956 à 1957. Durant cette période, Alger devint un véritable champ de bataille où le FLN et l'armée française se sont livrés à des combats sans merci. Les deux camps ont fait preuve d'une extrême violence, notamment lors des attentats commis par le FLN contre des innocents ou encore à travers les tortures pratiquées par l'armée française. Cette violence, que l'on ressent tout au long du film, est caractéristique des régimes coloniaux, mais surtout des débuts de révolutions. En effet, Frantz Fanon , dans Les Damnés de la Terre , explique que la violence est une étape nécessaire pour que le colonisé, privé de toute initiative et de libertés intérieures et extérieures, retrouve ses droits. La violence extrême est donc nécessaire, mais elle constitue seulement la première étape de la révolution, elle n'est pas la révolution en soi. Cette étape de la révolte et de la lutte armée est la forme infantile de la révolution, c'est-à-dire qu'elle constitue le premier mouvement nécessaire, mais qu'ensuite tout le travail reste à faire. La révolte permet d'arriver à l'indépendance dans le cas de l'Algérie, qui devient officiellement indépendante le 5 juillet 1962. Ce mouvement d'insurrection fut impossible à canaliser pour l'armée française, malgré sa supériorité militaire, c'est pourquoi De Gaulle conclut progressivement qu'une Algérie française n'était pas durable. C'est donc par la violence et le courage que l'Algérie devint indépendante. Comme le souligne Fanon , le plus dur dans la révolution est l'après-révolte : une fois que les opprimés ont gagné, que faut-il faire ? Comment s'organiser ? En Algérie, Ben Bella fut le premier président en 1963, mais il fut renversé en 1965 par un coup d'État. C'est ensuite Boumédiène qui prit la relève en renforçant le poids de l'État dans l'économie. Des politiques d'industrialisation (Industries industrialisantes ou modèle Feldman-Mahalanobis) furent mises en œuvre, mais avec un succès limité, car cette stratégie d'industrialisation est autocentrée et nécessite donc une forte demande intérieure. Or, en Algérie, la population représentait alors moins de 40 millions d'habitants. Cependant, grâce au pétrole et au gaz (95 % des recettes d'exportation algériennes), l'État a pu financer certains projets tout en restant fermé au tourisme et à une grande partie du commerce extérieur. Aujourd'hui, les relations franco-algériennes sont tendues. L'affaire Boualem Sansal en est un exemple. Il existe toujours des frictions entre les deux États, notamment autour du Sahara occidental et du passé colonial français.

texto: What impressed me most is that the movie refuses easy heroes. Both sides commit brutality. Both sides justify brutality. The French military often wins tactically. Raids, arrests, intelligence gathering, interrogations. The Algerian independence movement wins strategically. The film’s central point is devastatingly simple: An insurgency is not defeated when its fighters are defeated. It’s defeated when its cause loses legitimacy. The French win battles. Then lose Algeria. One of the rare war films that feels more interested in power and politics than victory.

tema: Abordagem de moralidade ambígua e falta de conclusão
exemplo: Algumas reviews medianas mencionam que o filme deixa a moralidade ambígua, sem dar uma resposta clara sobre o que é justo ou injusto, e que a narrativa parece questionar a própria abordagem sem chegar a uma conclusão definitiva.
texto: Got so excited because the music in this is used in Inglorious Basterds [45] On the technical level in regards to the psychology, camera-work, and thematic weight the depictions in this hold, this is an astoundingly well-done film. It has quite literally been used by both resistance fighters and militaries to gain insight on how these movements can be ran, it was written by someone who was a member of the FLN (National Liberation Front), contained actors who had lived through the accounts detailed, and was shot on location where the events occurred. There are of course some historical inaccuracies, but by and large this is a frighteningly accurate depiction of this event, and furthermore it makes you feel like you're there. It's also important to note that both the French authorities and FLN did even worse things in real life. Specifically the French, as this really cannot capture the breadth of killings and abuse they inflicted on Algerians to get their way (also highlights how useless the UN is and has always been). And there's one specific scene in this movie that is absolutely the highlight for me where Colonel Mathieu claims they cannot be fascists or oppressors as many of them were part of the resistance movement fighting against the Nazis ( cough couch Israel cough couch ). But this line is just wonderful, and for me it beautifully illuminates the uncomfortable reality of brutality humans are capable of; if our worldview justifies it we can be just as capable of the evils we decry. And this also gets into the meat of the question this film is proposing: what is justified in my fight for freedom? We are definitely on the side of the FLN in terms of perspective, but the film never tries to state that they are the good guys (and while I think we can come to the conclusion that comparatively they were, they still weren't "good" guys). It inherently puts the question to us when we are watching them bomb places with civilians of "is this justified?" Personally I don't know, I would like to say they could've instead bombed military targets or done some other thing, but the reality very well may be that this was the only way to make effective change (and when you are trying to change the fact that you are being brutally oppressed by colonizers, that effective change is pretty darn important). It's also interesting as they are fully willing to shirk things such as Sharia Law to wage this war (such as the women disguising themselves as French women) when the aim is to be able to reinstate that law once they have gained their independence (a whole other decision that I believe would warrant a whole new version of FLN to fight against the oppression that that brings). In the end I think this is wonderful at making you have to weigh what is right in your own mind, and hopefully reassess your own beliefs. At the very least this movie shines a light bulb on an event (and an issue) that deserves to be known and talked about. France still hasn't issued an apology to Algeria (just how the U.S. hasn't to Vietnam about things as basic as the effects of agent orange, or Japan to China about Nanjing, nor Britain to India, etc. etc.) and while I do believe the status of the world is much better today, it takes a simple Google to see this is still occurring all over. And I believe the biggest part that makes it overwhelmingly depressing is that it is truly completely manufactured by humans to a degree that is mind-numbingly pointless. So why am I giving this such a review after going over all that which I have gleamed from the movie? Cause I didn't really enjoy watching it that much. While all of the above are true, I never found myself caring about the events of the story. Characters are barely fleshed out, and they jump from person to person so quickly it's impossible to truly get invested in any particular aspect. The bag drop off scene is easily the best as it gives enough room to breathe and let you ruminate with the emotions of the characters, but outside of this it is purely the analytics of what is being done and the loud declaration of why (which is of course always for a free Algeria or because France doesn't want to give up Algeria) with no real inspection into the characters and deeper motivations. It sets me at a removed distance from what is going on, and I unfortunately could care little less what would happen to everyone. Of course I am sad when innocents die, but that is because innocents died, not because of anything the film was doing to invest me. Freedom isn't free, but what cost are we willing to pay, and what does free even truly mean to us?

Les deux camps ont fait preuve d'une extrême violence, notamment lors des attentats commis par le FLN contre des innocents ou encore à travers les tortures pratiquées par l'armée française. Cette violence, que l'on ressent tout au long du film, est caractéristique des régimes coloniaux, mais surtout des débuts de révolutions. En effet, Frantz Fanon , dans Les Damnés de la Terre , explique que la violence est une étape nécessaire pour que le colonisé, privé de toute initiative et de libertés intérieures et extérieures, retrouve ses droits. La violence extrême est donc nécessaire, mais elle constitue seulement la première étape de la révolution, elle n'est pas la révolution en soi. Cette étape de la révolte et de la lutte armée est la forme infantile de la révolution, c'est-à-dire qu'elle constitue le premier mouvement nécessaire, mais qu'ensuite tout le travail reste à faire. La révolte permet d'arriver à l'indépendance dans le cas de l'Algérie, qui devient officiellement indépendante le 5 juillet 1962. Ce mouvement d'insurrection fut impossible à canaliser pour l'armée française, malgré sa supériorité militaire, c'est pourquoi De Gaulle conclut progressivement qu'une Algérie française n'était pas durable. C'est donc par la violence et le courage que l'Algérie devint indépendante. Comme le souligne Fanon , le plus dur dans la révolution est l'après-révolte : une fois que les opprimés ont gagné, que faut-il faire ? Comment s'organiser ? En Algérie, Ben Bella fut le premier président en 1963, mais il fut renversé en 1965 par un coup d'État. C'est ensuite Boumédiène qui prit la relève en renforçant le poids de l'État dans l'économie. Des politiques d'industrialisation (Industries industrialisantes ou modèle Feldman-Mahalanobis) furent mises en œuvre, mais avec un succès limité, car cette stratégie d'industrialisation est autocentrée et nécessite donc une forte demande intérieure. Or, en Algérie, la population représentait alors moins de 40 millions d'habitants. Cependant, grâce au pétrole et au gaz (95 % des recettes d'exportation algériennes), l'État a pu financer certains projets tout en restant fermé au tourisme et à une grande partie du commerce extérieur. Aujourd'hui, les relations franco-algériennes sont tendues. L'affaire Boualem Sansal en est un exemple. Il existe toujours des frictions entre les deux États, notamment autour du Sahara occidental et du passé colonial français.

texto: Un excellent film où le cinéma d’action moderne est né. Un film politique du réalisateur italien Gillo Pontecorvo. La manière dont le film est produit est juste glaçante, même radicale. Basé sur la lutte pour l’indépendance algérienne, c’est un film qui brûle la rétine et le cœur du spectateur, assistant à cela jusqu’au point d’éveiller les consciences. Les acteurs sont bien choisis et ciblés de manière très précise. On ne cherche pas de grandes stars hollywoodiennes mais des visages de haine marqués par cet épisode colonial, qui retransmettent leur identité de combattant au téléspectateur. Les décors également, on veut de l’authenticité jusqu’au bout. On tourne dans la vraie Casbah d’Alger où, quelques années auparavant, des guérillas avaient véritablement eu lieu. Les plans également sont aussi un chef-d’œuvre. La caméra, tenue par Marcello Mastroianni, jette toutes les règles et tous les codes du monde du cinéma, filmant à portée de main pour nous introduire dans le monde réel qu’a vécu l’Algérie durant cette conquête coloniale. Il filme comme on court dans la Casbah, comment on se cache, comment on respire ainsi que l’on combat. Des cadres parfois instables, flous, mais totalement choisis pour l’immersion la plus totale, avec un vrai style tremblant de réalité. En conclusion, un film d’une expérience hors norme, nous faisant vibrer tout au long du visionnage, en comprenant la vie des algériens durant 132 ans de conquête coloniale sanglante menée par la France.

Lustigerweise aber wie „the Drama“ mit einem erstaunlich charmanten und berührenden Ende. Noch jemand Tee?

Instead of being an interesting exploration of relationships, it felt like it was pushing an idea I simply don't buy into. By the end it came across as another example of modern films prioritising social messaging over a compelling story. Definitely not my cup of tea.

texto: Takes time to find its legs. In the end it’s a very vanilla portrait of a marriage and couples in general. It will have an audience, but it missed me by a long shot. Some solid acting and decent writing, but it’s too understated in the wrong places and never as exciting as it thinks it is. I’d like to see a film about a relationship that’s dying, revives itself, but ultimately still falls apart. In a way the audience feels gut punched by because they thought they were going to make it.

texto: i found this to be insufferable for the first 2/3 of the movie. the acting was (mostly) good, there were very human moments, occasional funny moments, and some choices that compelled me. the score was fun, and i can tell they were trying to do some interesting things with blocking, but most shots felt repetitive and fell flat for me. ultimately, it felt like the writers and director focused so much on aesthetics and attempting to subvert the audience’s expectations that they neglected to develop a strong narrative i actually cared about and left me feeling like this was a patchwork of okay ideas that didn’t quite hit the mark in the end.

texto: Strange things are afoot in THE INVITE. I love movies that are basically just a play. tema: Atuações marcantes e química do elenco
exemplo: O elenco, incluindo Seth Rogen, Olivia Wilde, Penélope Cruz e Edward Norton, é elogiado por suas atuações intensas e química, com cada um trazendo profundidade e humor que se complementam no enredo.
texto: THE INVITE is an uproariously funny yet profoundly sad dramedy about a deteriorating couple who invite their sexually confident, free-spirited neighbors over for what’s meant to be a pleasant evening, only for it to spiral into something painfully awkward, ugly, and brutally honest. Seth Rogen showcases remarkable range, blending his signature comedy with the finest dramatic work of his career. Olivia Wilde delivers a soul-crushing performance fueled by anxiety and secondhand embarrassment, while her precise, assured direction turns this intimate chamber piece into an astounding seamless balancing act between humor and heartbreak with something meaningful to say about marriage and relationships. Edward Norton and Penélope Cruz are the cherry on top of what is a delicious offering from Wilde and easily the best directorial work of her career so far.

texto: Sundance Film Festival Presents: The Invite Directed By: Olivia Wilde Based on the Spanish film from 2020 called The People’s Upstairs directed by Cesc Gray. Joe and Angela is having a very tough time maintaining their relationship and one night in San Francisco their neighbors decided to come over of what could be a night to remember. Olivia Wilde wowed us in the 2019 film Booksmart which became an instant coming to age classic with one of the best comedic films in recent memory. Unfortunately I couldn’t say the same with her 2022 film Don’t Worry Darling which is a trainwreck of a movie and its production history behind it is a stuff of legends. After being in director jail for nearly 4 years, her next project is a smaller indie film is Based on the Spanish film from 2020 called The People’s Upstairs directed by Cesc Gray and it stars Seth Rogen, Olivia Wilde, Penelope Cruz and Edward Norton. So what do I think of the film, it’s a very provocative movie for adults that pays homage to the old school date movies. My only issue with the film is that the first 35-40 minutes didn’t find its footing yet and can feel a bit bloated at first but as soon as the comedy hits after those 35 minutes, the film eventually find its footing with some of the most silliest horniest scenes  during the film. Other than that issue, I do think this will be one of the most talked about films in the festival so far! Even though I like Seth Rogen and Olivia Wilde, it’s Penelope Cruz and Edward Norton’s show here that  I feel the film mostly worked because of their comedic timing and yet very horny character motives  that puts the film in insane situations. The film is also a one location film throughout the film and easily a very small cast but I feel the setting really create a far depressing tone that the film was going for and it worked for the most part. The Invite (2026) is easily one of this years Sundance’s better films so far! Even though it takes its time to get invested with the world and its characters, the film screenplay by Rashida Jones and Will McCormack gets better and gives uncomfortable horny jokes front and center and I feel Cruz and Norton understood the assignment the most. This is Wilde’s best film since Booksmart and easily the best directorial effort from Olivia Wilde that pays  homage to the old hangout films of the 1960s and 70s that managed to give the laughs and tears all throughout its official runtime.

texto: I wouldn’t be surprised if The Invite finds its way into multiple Oscar conversations. I already complimented my favorite aspects in my first review, but man, everything was so well done here. Today’s audience really liked the humor and I think Seth Rogen in particular balanced everything so well, including the humor and facial expressions. Being able to pull off a combination of one of the funniest and most tense movies of the year is special. The way they filmed it — the artsy opening sequence (which also perfectly comes full circle with the ending), the camera/lens choices, the color grading, and the way they framed the characters and utilized foreground and background blur — was so good. The color coordination too. I love how the opening scene goes from them being happy at an undisclosed time to the beautiful frames of Joe just being miserable. This film is an excellent psychological study on self and marriage — communication, opening up, your perspective on the things you have, and resentment. Joe had so many good things going for him, between his daughter, kids learning from him, his musical talent, a pretty wife, and a nice home in San Francisco. He chose to be hung up on the past and push people away. Angela just had communication issues and made Joe feel unheard. You also see that the seemingly perfect couple indeed had their own issues, but Hawk was able to apologize when he was wrong and it was easier for him to be vulnerable. It also just shows how someone like him — someone you could easily judge or put into a box because of his sex life — had his own life experiences that you could empathize with. The end is beautiful because music can really break down barriers and be a language of its own.

texto: Very amusing, beautiful and touching, it spoke to me in a surprisingly introspective way - and stayed with me for a while. It’s a funny, stage play-like movie, focused on its quatuor - not trying to throw too much else at you. It’s contained is what it is. But it’s definitely more than just filmed theatre though. The framing uses mirrors, windows, character positions to express relationships. The colours are meaningful and the photography allows for contrasting warm glows and colder settings. The film’s grain also adds to this timeless and familiar look, totally adapted for a domestic context. And the film spoke to me, made me reflect on my relationship, which was the cherry on the cake. I’ll say the jokes felt sometimes too exaggerated for the grounded characters - like the wine scene. Certain twists were predictable. Also you won’t convince me that Olivia Wilde can be someone who’s uncomfortable about her appearance, but maybe that’s just me. The soufflé bit killed me.

texto: Every inch of this film was designed to make the audience feel smart for reading into the “fine print” that was actually neon signs. Every single one of the 1000 narrative payoffs was BEGGING to be recognized as a whisper instead of a shout, and I reckon most of the public did exactly so, given the rating. But it said it itself: “you don’t really want to work it out, you want to be fooled”. It’s so presumptuous, you could feel Nolan’s finger pointing at the threads he opened and hollering “LOOK LOOK THAT’S AN IMPORTANT DETAIL and then you can brag that you saw it coming”. Just essentially a kids movie. The cherry on the top of this big nothing cake is the theme of the film, what was it? Magic, obsession, supernatural? It switches up so fast I can’t seem to get a picture. They compete for their importance in the film and not a singular idea was developed, not a single idea won. No one won and the loser is the audience being tricked into thinking it’s smart by Nolan’s infantile attempt of directing what could have been a good film.

texto: I sat with it to see if I liked it more, but it just kept getting worse. At first, it tried to say something on obsession and its effects, especially when it leads to actions that make you question the morality of the characters. Which would've been very interesting if any of the characters were developed enough for you to even care. None of them feel like actual living people. Their actions carry no weight because there was no established ground for them to be based off of. They exist for the sole purpose of spouting corny one liners and making the most retarded and nonsensical decisions just to force the plot in the direction that Nolan wants. None of the events that happened evoke any sort of emotion in me besides being frustrated at how stupid and nonsensical all the characters are. So instead of these ideas being given the proper time and care to be fleshed out and explored, they get buried under the countless cheesy one-liners and stupidly and forcibly convoluted plotlines, to the point where they become unrecognisable by the end of the movie. When I finished it, I had no idea what was I supposed to get out of it, and after sitting on it, I'm even more confused. It all got sacrificed for the sake of setting up the plot twists at the end, which served nothing but be plot twists for the sake of being plot twists. If anything, they made the story worse. You needn't think for more than five seconds to recognise how stupid the ending is. The movie would've worked much better as a comedy rather than a cat-and-mouse-chase-esque thriller. Long story short, it insists upon itself.

exemplo: Algumas críticas criticam a direção por ser excessivamente explicativa e pretensiosa, e a atuação por sofrer com o excesso de diálogos e a falta de naturalidade.
texto: This is definitionally High Camp but because it somehow pertains to straight male culture it is not considered as such and that friction is a big part of why our culture’s usage of the word camp pisses me off but that’s a different subject. The opening shot being the cemetery of top hats, I instantly cackled! And then winced because the sound effects where so loud but the dialogue barely audible! How are you meant to watch this without subtitles?! What I think is fascinating is truly how every aspect of this film exemplifies the idea of failed seriousness but because it was made by a posh autistic British man we are meant to think of it as elevated. The way it tells you the plot in the first minute (and also that it follows a very classic narrative three part act because that’s what films are!), the performances and the accents are insanely over the top, the terrible wigs and prosthetic hair pieces, it’s all just very silly. But it treats this silliness with the utmost seriousness which I think is really funny but it also saps any Levity out of it. It’s a dour, very heavy handed drama for Harry Potter adults that, ironically for the subject matter, almost compulsively tells rather than shows you. I think there is something inherently so telling about choosing to make a film about prestidigitation where all magic is “logical” or at least scientific. Because those type of magicians are ontologically opposed to the idea of natural magic, predicated on the need for explanation. I think this film prefigures so much of the current horrors with its damn flashbacks, the way everyone constantly announces their intentions and how women are nothing but plot contrivances (Rebecca Hall you deserved better than this and the second you appeared on screen I instantly got sad for the unceremonious way you were ineluctably doomed to get fridged) I think I will just never understand why people revere Nolan, I find his filmmaking so clunky and laden footed and I can’t really understand this obsession with making everything so self serious even though you pick quite silly themes or subjects but hey! I guess I’m just left with how much I loathe how Christian Bale holds his mouth in this and I could never see anything else in his scenes

texto: After watching a bunch of nolan’s films consecutively, I have come to realise I really don’t gaf about the troubles of men who have left nothing but destruction in their path. The films always position themselves as a lesson that actions have consequences, but if the consequence is the loss of something so poorly written and badly fleshed out, the audience doesn’t actually understand the gravity of it. For example, if the lead’s wife dies, the assumption of his pain lies purely in our understanding of love and marriage. It does not depend on the actual film at all, and that’s where the films fall flat. Been trying to pinpoint what exactly makes the films so shallow and hollow, and now I finally do. All it took was being imprisoned on a plane which meant unwavering concentration to the content I was consuming. Oh also, I think I saw Dev Patel as an extra at some point.

tema: Trilha sonora e direção de Christopher Nolan
exemplo: Várias reviews medianas apontam que o estilo de direção de Nolan, com sua narrativa não linear e uso de truques, é complexo demais e quebra a tensão, tornando a experiência arrastada e pouco envolvente.
texto: My least favorite narrative device is opening on the ending and then spending the movie showing us how we got there, and The Prestige leans hard into exactly that. More than anything, though, it’s surprisingly joyless and humorless. For a movie about magic, showmanship, and entertainment, there’s very little sense of wonder or fun. Everyone is miserable, everyone is obsessed, and the movie treats every moment with enormous seriousness. There are good performances, the period setting works, and the central rivalry has its moments. But for all the tricks and twists, this is far from Nolan at his best.

texto: This movie could have had so much to say. In seeking to hurt others we often destroy ourselves. The consciousness of a person that has basically become a real life human Theseus’s ship. Two men destroying each other to the point of no return, in an equal measure, because London can only be big enough for one of them. It stopped being about a trick long ago, it was about proving to each other, not the audience, they could always up the ante. But instead it chooses, till the very end and much to my annoyance, to remain a dick measuring contest . Next time, get a ruler out, it’ll be faster. Maybe I would’ve been less cynical if I saw this in 2006. Alas, 20 years later… I see a movie that mostly disappoints with flat characters and so little actual magic that it’s not enough for me to forgive how much it overall annoyed me.

texto: Nunca entendiste cuál era el fin. El publico sabe la verdad. El mundo es simple, miserable, es despiadadamente real. Pero si podías embaucarlos sólo un segundo, se hacian preguntas. Entonces conseguías ver algo especial. Esa mirada atónita en sus caras Me considero una persona muy interesada en la magia y a la cual le gusta ver trucos e intentar descifrarlos. Esta película más allá de usar ciencia ficción, también usa y revela trucos que se han llegado a hacer en la vida real y eso siento que enriquece mucho a la obra. Una vez más, se trata el tema de la obsesión y de querer ser el mejor o el más reconocido en un ámbito. Y, como ya es sabido, estos comportamientos no suelen acabar bien. En cuanto a la rivalidad entre los magos, me ha gustado mucho. Hay un motivo verdadero y de peso por el cual terminan así el uno con el otro. A partir de ahí, es un sinfín de manipulaciones el uno al otro, hasta que llega a su fin de un modo u otro. Centrándome un poco en la narrativa, a pesar de haber visto este recurso anteriormente de manera continua, siento que a esta película en concreto le viene muy bien. Hasta el último minuto de la película he tenido preguntas que se han resuelto en ese mismo momento y que me han dejado asombrado. En general he disfrutado bastante de esta película y estoy más que satisfecho. Aunque me hubiera gustado haber visto algún truco de cartas que conozco.

texto: Es una historia brillante, mira que yo odio cuando una historia te miente a la cara para desarrollar su giro argumental y que no te des cuenta, pero es que esta la hace con fundamento, es la gracia del giro, que sea imposible esperartelo, es literalmente un truco de magia que abarca toda la película. Absolutamente brillante está historia, maravillosa. Tengo igualmente dos quejas con la película, una de ellas es que la parte en la que Robert intenta copiar el truco del hombre transportado y se junta con su parecido, como el mismo actor hace de los dos personajes hubieron algunas partes que me confundía un poco sobre quien era el verdadero Robert, sobretodo cuando avanza más la película y empiezan a apetecer que si clones y teletransporte real, ahí no paraba de pensar en ese parecido de Robert cuando en realidad nunca más lo volvieron a usar. Y la otra queja diría que bastante menor, es todo el rollo de los clones de Robert y la maquina de Tesla, no me parece mal para nada, solo que no me pega con todo lo demás de la película, entiendo que esto haga falta para como se desarrolla el giro final pero cuando todos los trucos en la historia han sido efectuados usando la maña, cuando un truco es magia y ciencia ficción literal pues me desconecto un poco con la película. Para terminar. Todos los demás aspectos de la película cumplen bastante bien, aunque obviamente su fuerte sea el guión y la historia, lo demás no se siente menos trabajado y para añadir, el casting es una maravilla.

texto: The Prestige is one of those films that gets better the more you think about it. The rivalry between the two magicians is already beautiful but the plot twist completely changes how you see everything that came before it. Nolan gives you the answer right in front of you while making you believe you’re looking somewhere else. The ending is honestly one of the most satisfying twists I’ve seen because it doesn’t just shock you it makes the entire movie make sense in a completely different way.

texto: There’s a sort of irony that, despite being a beyond exceptional technical directing talent who only gained the assistance of even more exceptional technical directing talent along the way, Iñárritu is by far the most graceless, hollow showboater Hollywood has seen in decades, arguably even more than someone as derided for showboating as Michael Bay. He’s a monkey’s paw curse made man: born with both divine technical ability and the worst possible thematic and narrative instincts those technical abilities could be paired with. Derivative, overly-literal macho faux-art nonsense. Historically irresponsible, burdened with clunky attempts at spiritualist visual metaphor and just way, waaaaaay too long. Lubezki can light and shoot snow-covered forests and babbling brooks all day but he can’t save a movie that, at its core, has nothing of any worth to say. Nothing truly relevant or engaging happens between those beautifully composed frames, save for a final shot that attempts to add deeper subtext the narrative itself does not attempt to possess. If you're after a “man fights nature/masculinity” movie set in a lot of snowy forest wildernesses that’s actually good, Joe Carnahan’s “The Grey” is a daring masterpiece.

texto: Leonardo DiCaprio gehört zweifelsohne zu den besten  US-amerikanischen Schauspielern der Gegenwart. Lange musste er trotz einer beeindruckenden Filmografie auf den längst verdienten Oscar als Bester Haupdarsteller warten. Umso trauriger, dass er mit diesem für  den Rachewestern "The Revenant" ausgezeichnet wurde. Von der großartigen Schauspielkunst DiCaprios ist hier hinter seinem Bart und unter dem Schnee leider wenig zu sehen. Seine Leinwandkollegen Tom Hardy oder die Grizzlybärin können diesen auch nicht übertreffen. Der von DiCaprio verkörperte Hugh Glass und der Pferdekadaver sind auch kein gutes Leinwandpaar. Dass DiCaprio sowie Regiesseur Alejandro González Iñárritu für diesen Film jeweils mit dem Oscar ausgezeichnet wurden, bestätigt noch einmal die Blut, Schweiß und Tränen-Ideologie der Academy.  Survival-Challenges oder dass man als Vegetarier rohe Bisonleber verspeist, scheinen wohl Merkmale guter Schauspielkunst zu sein. Es wirkt, als sei dieser Film vor allem gemacht worden, um bei der Oscarverleihung 2016 abzuräumen. Sieht man mal von den Schauspielern ab, hat der Film weder oberflächlich noch inhaltlich etwas zu bieten. Die Handlung ist banal und die Landschaftsaufnahmen erinnern eher an den Windows-Sperrbildschirm als an großes Western-Kino. Die Suche nach Spiritualität wirkt aufgesetzt, um der Handlung künstlich Tiefe zu verleihen. Es hätte ja ein interessanter Film sein können, der das Verhältnis von Mensch und Natur und die Themen und Fragen des Western-Genres aufgreift und neu verhandelt. Doche solche Fragen und Genre-Motive sind hier eher lose Assoziationen als bedeutungstragende Elemente des Films. Möglicherweise wird "The Revenant" nur dafür in Erinnerung bleiben, dass Leonardo DiCaprio für diesen Film seinen bisher einzigen Oscar als Bester Hauptdarsteller gewann.

texto: Infelizmente é muito forçado. Iñárritu está desesperado aqui, gritando para o telespectador que o que ele coloca em tela é MUITO FODA, ÉPICO, BRILHANTE, zero sutileza. Parece que depois de Birdman ele se perdeu na carreira. Filme pretensioso, mas que de certa forma é vazio. Se isso fosse luta livre, diríamos que é extremamente OVERBOOKADO, tirando a iluminação, nada parece natural, é tudo montado para gerar sofrimento, miséria e barreiras para o protagonista, para também canonizar como alguém bom e moral, esse é o principal motivo para a existência dos nativos no longa, aliás. Estilo e padrão estético elevado tem, claro. A fotografia é insana, o jeito que é filmado também. Gosto do jeito que lembra um videogame de sobrevivência em alguns momentos, é uma baita experiência e tem grandes cenas, sufocantes e tensas, como o do ataque da ursa, mas isso por si só não faz um bom filme. Eu nem digo que achei totalmente ruim, mas obra que está mais preocupada em se vender como arte do que realmente ser, não me pega muito.

texto: Ignorndo el complejo de salvador blanco que tiene esta película, resulta siendo una obra difícil de olvidar, sea por las bellísimas locaciones, la crudeza del guión, el oso cgi o la actuación de Leonardo DiCaprio que le hizo ganar su Oscar. La dirección de fotografía junto a las locaciones de la película hacen que estés las dos horas y media admirando el valor escénico de la película, que termina siendo lo más rescatable en mi opinión. Tom Hardy hizo un trabajo tan bueno que no supe que está en la película hasta que vi los créditos finales. The Revenant es una película evidentemente hecha para DiCaprio, todos escuchamos sobre el trabajo de preparación que hizo para el papel aprendiendo lenguas nativo-americanas, técnicas de supervivencia, etc, pero si esta información no se hubiera hecho pública, la actuación de DiCaprio habría terminado siendo otro casi-Oscar. Leonardo necesitaba un papel para un hombre blanco sensible y se lo dieron. La dirección de fotografía y storyboard carrean completamente a The Revenant.

The acting chops on display here are also top notch, with DiCaprio, Hardy and Poulter all being standouts. Watching him get destroyed by a bear was epic and there is a lot of scenes in this that look great. Overall I was kinda disappointed and confused in this but it isn’t bad. If you want a solid movie with minimal dialogue then this is a pretty good option. If you want to watch it solely for the Leo performance and what you expected this to be then I wouldn’t watch it. When I first started the movie I was a little confused about what was going on and asked myself why did I chose to watch this. I was kinda second guessing my decision to watch this after it started but I realized this movie isn’t that bad. I don’t know why I just kept thinking to myself that this is a 1800s John wick. Not a bad movie but also not as good as expected.

exemplo: As atuações de Leonardo DiCaprio e Tom Hardy são frequentemente mencionadas como um dos aspectos mais fortes do filme. Apesar de alguns considerarem que a performance de DiCaprio não é sua melhor, a força de Hardy no papel de antagonista é destacada como um fator que salva a obra.
texto: Ignorndo el complejo de salvador blanco que tiene esta película, resulta siendo una obra difícil de olvidar, sea por las bellísimas locaciones, la crudeza del guión, el oso cgi o la actuación de Leonardo DiCaprio que le hizo ganar su Oscar. La dirección de fotografía junto a las locaciones de la película hacen que estés las dos horas y media admirando el valor escénico de la película, que termina siendo lo más rescatable en mi opinión. Tom Hardy hizo un trabajo tan bueno que no supe que está en la película hasta que vi los créditos finales. The Revenant es una película evidentemente hecha para DiCaprio, todos escuchamos sobre el trabajo de preparación que hizo para el papel aprendiendo lenguas nativo-americanas, técnicas de supervivencia, etc, pero si esta información no se hubiera hecho pública, la actuación de DiCaprio habría terminado siendo otro casi-Oscar. Leonardo necesitaba un papel para un hombre blanco sensible y se lo dieron. La dirección de fotografía y storyboard carrean completamente a The Revenant.

texto: The script is simple: revenge after injustice. The movie is built around the pain and suffering of Hugh Glass, who has his stepson killed by Fitzgerald after their settlement is attacked by Native Americans. A premise like that demands great performances to make an impact, and that's what holds the entire movie together. DiCaprio delivers it pretty well. It isn't one of his best performances, but it's a good one. Unpopular opinion: I believe Tom Hardy is the standout of the entire film! I don't usually expect much from him, and that's exactly why his performance is so impressive. Maybe the best character he has ever played. The whole time he is on screen, he grabs your attention. Simply as that. We've all seen dozens of revenge movies, but DiCaprio and, mainly, Hardy make this one stand out. The direction is great, and the scenes are raw, bloody, and aggressive. The soundtrack is subtle but works well. In short: the movie is simple, well-paced, and well-structured, and Hardy's performance makes it even cooler. OBS: DiCaprio has played several characters better than this one. It's kind of sad that "The Revenant" was the role that finally won him the award in 2016.

texto: Infelizmente é muito forçado. Iñárritu está desesperado aqui, gritando para o telespectador que o que ele coloca em tela é MUITO FODA, ÉPICO, BRILHANTE, zero sutileza. Parece que depois de Birdman ele se perdeu na carreira. Filme pretensioso, mas que de certa forma é vazio. Se isso fosse luta livre, diríamos que é extremamente OVERBOOKADO, tirando a iluminação, nada parece natural, é tudo montado para gerar sofrimento, miséria e barreiras para o protagonista, para também canonizar como alguém bom e moral, esse é o principal motivo para a existência dos nativos no longa, aliás. Estilo e padrão estético elevado tem, claro. A fotografia é insana, o jeito que é filmado também. Gosto do jeito que lembra um videogame de sobrevivência em alguns momentos, é uma baita experiência e tem grandes cenas, sufocantes e tensas, como o do ataque da ursa, mas isso por si só não faz um bom filme. Eu nem digo que achei totalmente ruim, mas obra que está mais preocupada em se vender como arte do que realmente ser, não me pega muito.

texto: This has been on my watchlist since it came out and my friend braved the theaters with a box of chicken tenders she had to throw away because the violence made it inedible. I might have a different threshold for violence because despite the blood and gore, the only thing particularly shocking to me is that we are still making movies in which members of the indigenous population die so the white man can have motivation to carry him through each narrative beat. This movie is visually stunning. I love when the landscape becomes a character in and of itself and some of the cinematography is downright beautiful. I also loved the visceral camera work. You are zoomed unflatteringly close to faces or kicked aside in very smooth camerwork that anchors you in the action and splatters the camera lens. But I also had to suspend a lot of disbelief for this one. The human body can survive a lot, but . . . let's be real. He should have died like 10+ times. Infection, blood loss, blunt force trauma, hypothermia . . . Dude had a lot of ways out and somehow had enough energy to lug that soggy bear pelt around. (Also, how fast do hides cure?)
