texto: I did it! I watched The Revenant! What did I get out of the experience, you ask? First things first: Naughty Dog and Rockstar should be bending their knees to Iñárritu after ripping off their respective climactic fights from this film. The Revenant: probably in the upper echelon of "films I've never seen despite my age and preferences in actors and Oscar history." I remember watching the commercials before its release, but I was too young at the time to go see it (or at least too young to want to witness Leo crawl into the belly of a stallion). I have fond memories of the "Leo has never won an Oscar" memes, and endlessly watched WatchMojo's incessantness in crowning him in the number one spot for Oscarless movie stars. Despite my desire, the half-face Leo staring into the lens of the camera poster never caught my eye enough on streaming services to warrant a click (the 150-minute runtime doesn't help either, but this is also the guy who watched Oppenheimer 6 times, so take that claim with a grain of salt). Thank god HBO Max decided to blow the dust off of their Digger-related media this month. I've already watched Birdman, and I've started The Last Samurai (which doesn't look to be passing the Woke-ometer based on the first half hour). I'm taking the opportunity given to me and consuming myself with all the knowledge I can before the first of next month, when my most anticipated movie of the year comes out (It's Verity). A decade of buildup, the final episode when I finally watch the movie- does it live up to the hype I've built up in my mind... Um... Eh. Remember in The Last Jedi when they act like they're going to kill off Leia, and give her this really beautiful swan song scene, only to have her survive the attack and then never speak again throughout the rest of the trilogy. Like, yeah, that was all good and dandy, but what's the point? That's how I feel about The Revenant. Sure, Leo gives a great performance, the camera work is electric, and the cinematography is beautiful, but what does any of it amount to other than meeting those specified criteria? Why does The Revenant exist? Is it commenting on some greater cultural theme that 2015 audiences could resonate with? I don't see any. Is it trying to be an Odyssey-esque revenge story for Leo to shine in? I guess, but it doesn't do anything particularly unique besides replacing the Cyclops with a bear. I just see no reason for this movie to exist other than to watch people's eyes open in bewildered awe as you explain to them the basic plot points of the film. Happy for Leo, worried about Digger.

Another Leonardo DiCaprio movie ticked off the list, and once again he gives such an incredible performance. It won’t go down as one of my favourite movies ever, but it was still a really good watch and definitely worth finally ticking off the list!

texto: "The Revenant" es la película modelo que deberían seguir todos los directores si quieren conseguir que su actor principal gane un Óscar. Para empezar, la trama es emocionantísima y deja momentos de una tensión brutal, como la pelea con el oso, en la que de verdad estás sufriendo mientras la ves. Además, a medida que avanza la historia, se va haciendo cada vez más evidente la diferencia entre los personajes que rodean al protagonista y el propio Hugh Glass, que acaba dejando escenas que quedan para la memoria. Más cosas que quiero reseñar de esta cinta son: • La actuación: Leonardo DiCaprio, dando vida a Hugh Glass, está brutal. Es una actuación de Óscar y está a un nivel estratosférico. Consigue transmitir muchísimo prácticamente sin necesidad de palabras y hace que sientas todo lo que está viviendo el personaje. El resto del elenco también está muy bien, aunque algunos aparecen durante tan poco tiempo en pantalla que no tienen suficiente margen para demostrar todo su potencial. • La dirección: Alejandro G. Iñárritu es un genio absoluto de la dirección. La manera en la que utiliza los planos consigue que el protagonista luzca todavía más y que cada momento tenga una fuerza visual enorme. La cámara está constantemente encima de los personajes y hace que vivas las situaciones prácticamente desde dentro, demostrando el enorme talento de Iñárritu detrás de las cámaras.

texto: Revisiting this almost ten years after I first reviewed it, and my impression hasn't budged: same admiration, same reservations, same grade. This is a film that demands something from you, and the rewatch was every bit as punishing as I remembered. Not a flaw, a design. The cold, the length, the sheer physical exhaustion of Glass dragging himself back to life all become something you endure rather than simply watch. On the technical side it is close to flawless. Iñárritu's direction is staggering, and Lubezki shooting on nothing but natural light gives you images you don't forget. DiCaprio throws his whole body into a nearly wordless role and finally got the Oscar he'd been chasing, with Tom Hardy just as good as the treacherous Fitzgerald. The lifelike makeup seals the immersion. Everything you can point a camera at, or build in front of one, is working at the highest level. Where it falls short is the script. The pacing sags in stretches, and too many scenes seem to exist for their visual force rather than any real narrative weight, beauty that doesn't always serve the whole. It's a monumental thing to behold and a hard one to sit through, and I respect it more than I love it. A survival epic that earns its greatness and makes you pay for every minute of it.

exemplo: Várias reviews medianas criticam o roteiro por parecer pouco incisivo na construção das personagens, com alguns personagens como Jéssica sendo considerados rasos ou mal desenvolvidos, o que prejudica a narrativa.
texto: A pessoa já nasce sabendo, o que pode e o que não pode. Essa frase me marcou muito em Que Horas Ela Volta? , pois aqui é onde chegamos mais próximos do filme nos mostrar a raiz de todo o problema que a narrativa da obra nos sugere. Em outras palavras, por mais que saibamos que isso não é verdade, nos é imposto enquanto classe não dominante, desde que nascemos, que “naturalmente” temos um lugar definido na sociedade e que podemos até ascender, melhorar de vida, fazer “parte da família”, mas nunca estar no mesmo plano, mesmo lugar, mesma posição que a classe dominante, jamais. E é nesse contexto que trago o primeiro grande ponto positivo do filme: os enquadramentos. À Val, empregada da família, só lhe pertence um pequeno espaço, a cozinha, o quartinho pequeno e quente da empregada. Ela enxerga seus patrões através de uma parede que os divide, e portanto define muito bem o lugar de cada um. Ela só se junta a eles para servir e nada mais. No quarto dela, a câmera a filma atrás de uma grade, pois ela está presa e vulnerável dentro desse sistema. E o pior: por achar que é algo natural, que as coisas sempre foram assim, ela acaba acreditando que a vida dela é essa sem possibilidade de mudança. Ela cuida do filho dos patrões como se fosse seu, cuida da casa deles como se fosse sua, ela cuida de uma vida que não é dela e em troca deixa a própria vida e sua família de lado. Tudo isso por um valor financeiro baixo, injusto e explorado. É cruel. Mas aí entra o que seria o ponto-chave da virada: Jéssica, a filha de Val, vem para a cidade grande prestar vestibular e morar com a mãe (a quem mal consegue chamar de mãe, visto que Val teve que abdicar da própria família para ganhar a vida). Esse era para ser o grande motor de conscientização, mas, na minha visão, a personagem de Jéssica acaba sendo mal conduzida pelo roteiro. Não se trata apenas de uma rebeldia ou arrogância juvenil - o que seria compreensível, mas de uma falha no objetivo narrativo claro da personagem. Jéssica é pintada como extremamente inteligente, mas suas tentativas de conscientizar a mãe se resumem a gestos vazios, como dizer que ela pode entrar na piscina ou comer na mesa dos patrões, por exemplo. O que isso muda de fato no problema de classe? Na realidade material, se uma empregada doméstica decide usar a piscina dos patrões, ou ela sofre uma repreensão severa (afinal, eles detêm o poder financeiro e, por consequência, o poder sobre ela), ou é sumariamente demitida e substituída. Reduzir a emancipação de classe a esses "favores permitidos" esvazia a crítica. As falas e atitudes da Jéssica acabam soando rasas diante da grandiosidade do conflito que o próprio filme propõe. Obs: minha crítica quanto a isso é justamente a premissa narrativa política do filme, isso é esvaziado, raso, quase deixado de lado ao longo do filme. Ilustrando: A cena em que Bárbara, mãe da família, manda esvaziar a piscina depois que Jéssica entrou, falando que achou que tinha visto um rato ali é repugnante, é nojenta, dá raiva, mas isso no roteiro do filme não é explorado mais profundamente, não dá pra entender. Outra coisa que me incomodou: As cenas do pai da família com a Jéssica são muito constrangedoras também, até entendo o pensamento delas terem existido (hipocrisia e a objetificação velada da elite progressista…), mas mais uma vez cenas mal escritas e que no fim também ficaram sem sentido. O final também não me agrada, fica uma sensação de resolução simples que não resolve nada, afinal, se demitir do emprego explorador para finalmente viver mais de perto a sua própria vida junto de sua família, faz você de fato sair do sistema que anteriormente te fez abdicar de tudo isso? Não existe outra solução para ter uma vida mais digna junto das pessoas que você ama? Agora, o ponto alto do filme realmente é Val. Regina Casé brilhou aqui, personagem bem escrita demais, o filme é inteiramente dela. Fico de certa forma feliz de ter demorado um pouco pra ver esse filme, pois agora tive a oportunidade de assisti-lo com um olhar mais radicalizado politicamente. O capitalismo, como sempre a raiz do problema, dilacera famílias, criando um ciclo eterno de meninos e meninas perguntando “Que horas ela volta?” Um filme muito bom em expor o problema, mas pouco incisivo em mostrar a raiz, as soluções e uma conscientização mais crua dessa mesma questão. Ps: Adorei o fato de terem mostrado que o pai da família herdou tudo o que tem, ou seja, nos mostra que várias dessas famílias ricas e da elite herdaram seu patrimônio. Em outras palavras, essas pessoas não produzem nada, não trabalham, são vagabundas e vivem da exploração do trabalho alheio. 6,8/10

exemplo: Algumas reviews medianas apontam que a fotografia e o enquadramento poderiam ser melhor trabalhados, com cenas que parecem desnecessárias ou que não contribuem de forma eficaz para o desenvolvimento da história.
texto: U ma empregada doméstica que passou anos trabalhando na casa de uma família em São Paulo vê a rotina que construiu ali ser atravessada pela chegada da própria filha, com quem não convive há dez anos desde que precisou deixá-la para trás para trabalhar. A partir desse reencontro, o filme reorganiza tudo o que parecia estável: o vínculo entre patrões e funcionária, os limites daquela casa, a forma como cada personagem ocupa o espaço e, principalmente, a maneira como essa mulher aprendeu a existir dentro de uma estrutura que exige intimidade, mas nunca oferece pertencimento de verdade. O que mais me pegou no filme foi justamente a contradição que sustenta a personagem central. Para sobreviver, ela precisou se afastar da filha e transformar o cuidado em trabalho. Só que, no processo, esse cuidado foi deslocado para dentro da casa de outra família. Ela cozinha, organiza, acolhe, escuta, participa da rotina, ajuda a criar o filho dos patrões e se torna uma presença afetiva indispensável naquele espaço. Existe algo muito duro na forma como o filme expõe essa inversão: enquanto a maternidade da protagonista foi interrompida pela necessidade de trabalhar, a casa em que ela serve passa a absorver justamente esse afeto que faltou em outro lugar. E o filme entende bem a força desse deslocamento. A relação dela com o filho dos patrões não é construída como um excesso melodramático, mas como resultado de convivência, repetição e presença. Quando o menino precisa de acolhimento, é nela que ele encontra isso. Ao mesmo tempo, a mãe biológica, embora esteja fisicamente presente e cercada de conforto, parece incapaz de estabelecer com o próprio filho a mesma intimidade. O cuidado, aqui, deixa de ser apenas uma função doméstica e passa a operar também como vínculo, como afeto e como substituição silenciosa de ausências. A chegada da filha da protagonista é o elemento que rompe essa lógica. Ela entra naquela casa sem reproduzir o comportamento de adaptação que a mãe aprendeu a naturalizar. Questiona limites, ocupa espaços, desafia códigos implícitos e, com isso, torna visível uma hierarquia que até então funcionava quase em silêncio. Em alguns momentos, essa postura pode soar agressiva ou até insolente, mas o filme dá material suficiente para que ela seja lida de forma mais complexa. Existe ali uma jovem que cresceu longe da mãe, sem intimidade real com aquela relação, e que não reconhece automaticamente as regras emocionais e sociais que organizam aquela casa. Quando ela diz que não se acha melhor que ninguém, apenas não se acha pior, o filme encontra uma das suas sínteses mais fortes. Esse embate entre mãe e filha me parece um dos pontos mais interessantes da narrativa justamente porque ele não se reduz a um choque de temperamentos. O conflito também nasce de uma lacuna. A distância entre as duas não é apenas física, mas formativa. Falta convivência, falta repertório de afeto, falta o tempo que foi consumido pelo trabalho e nunca pôde ser vivido dentro daquela relação. Isso dá à personagem da filha uma função muito importante: ela não apenas tensiona a estrutura da casa, mas também devolve à mãe uma imagem desconfortável da vida que foi sendo normalizada ao longo dos anos. A minha maior reserva com o filme está menos no que ele quer dizer e mais em como ele organiza formalmente tudo isso. As ideias são fortes, o recorte é muito claro e a dinâmica entre os personagens funciona, mas em alguns momentos eu senti falta de uma execução mais refinada. A direção aposta num naturalismo discreto, com uma encenação muito funcional, e isso às vezes concentra o peso do filme quase todo no roteiro e nas atuações. Para mim, faltou em certos trechos uma elaboração visual mais forte, algo que tensionasse melhor o espaço, os deslocamentos e as relações de poder que o filme está o tempo inteiro colocando em cena. Senti isso especialmente na forma como a passagem do tempo é tratada. As transições são secas, pouco marcadas, e embora seja possível ler isso como uma escolha da diretora para sugerir um tempo que escapa à personagem, um tempo consumido pela rotina e pelo trabalho, na prática isso nem sempre me convenceu. Em vez de ampliar o impacto dramático dessa perda, em alguns momentos a narrativa me passou mais uma sensação de transição abrupta do que propriamente de construção. Eu entendo o que o filme talvez queira fazer ali, mas nem sempre acho que funciona. Também me chamou atenção a figura do marido da patroa, que aparece como uma presença meio frouxa, mas importante para a atmosfera daquela casa. Ele ajuda a expor o desgaste afetivo daquele núcleo familiar e adiciona outra camada de desconforto à dinâmica da protagonista com aquele ambiente. Não é um personagem desenvolvido em profundidade, mas a maneira como ele circula pelo filme reforça a sensação de que aquela casa inteira opera sobre vínculos frágeis, carências mal resolvidas e afetos deslocados. Ainda assim, nada disso apaga a força do filme. Que Horas Ela Volta ? continua sendo um filme muito preciso naquilo que observa, especialmente quando acompanha o lugar ambíguo que essa mulher ocupa dentro da casa dos patrões e o modo como a chegada da filha obriga essa estrutura a se revelar. Talvez eu não ache que a execução alcance, o tempo todo, a potência do material que tem nas mãos. Mas o que o filme constrói em torno dessa personagem, da sua rotina e do seu desgaste, permanece forte o bastante para sustentar o impacto. No fim, o que fica para mim é menos a sensação de ruptura e mais a de deslocamento. Como se aquela mulher, aos poucos, começasse a perceber que a vida dela não precisava continuar restrita ao papel que passou anos exercendo dentro da casa dos outros. E talvez a força do desfecho esteja justamente aí: não em transformar essa saída num grande gesto dramático, mas em tratá-la como um movimento tardio de retomada, quase silencioso, de uma vida que há muito tempo vinha sendo vivida em função de todo mundo, menos dela mesma.

texto: Minha professora de redação passou uma parte desse filme na quarta-feira e hoje me bateu a curiosidade para terminar de assistir. É realmente muito bom na crítica! Dá para ser usado como repertório em várias redações O que me deixou um pouco desconfortável em relação à produção desse longa foi a atuação. Acho que os atores não expressaram tão bem alguns sentimentos, com exceção, é claro, da Regina Casé. Além da atuação, achei algumas cenas meio desnecessárias para o contexto do filme, cenas estas, que, na minha opinião, facilmente seriam descartadas.

texto: O filme tem uma progressão bem lenta e acho que esse efeito se intensifica por conta de um roteiro ordinário, não é ruim mas também nada que faça você pensar nele como uma super obra. Ele peca em tentar desenvolver os personagens e no fim deixar todos meio abertos, com exceção da Val que realmente foi a estrela do filme; a evolução dessa personagem é incrível de assistir, a maneira como ela vai se libertando e percebendo as coisas é feito com cuidado e tempo. A atuação não é lá essas coisas, tanto que na minha visão os momentos em que deveria ter um peso enorme, acabou virando cenas simples, sem muita emoção. A cena da piscina foi acho que o ápice, eu fiquei felizinha pela Val e as cenas depois dessas então eu tava "é isso mesmo Val você merece mais!". Enfim, um filme que valhe a pena de assistir

texto: Quão estruturadas são as coisas em nosso país. Eu poderia falar de mundo mas quero especificar a realidade do Brasil como é especificado no filme. Estruturado significa algo organizado, bem arrumado ou que tem uma base firme, regras e costumes invisíveis que já fazem parte do funcionamento normal da sociedade. O preconceito está tão enraizado nas regras e tradições que parece ser algo "natural" ou normal do dia a dia. Em "Que horas ela volta" vemos a Val tão intrinsecamente infiltrada nessa realidade que ela mesma comete certas vezes esse preconceito estrutural sem querer, porque para ela é normal. Ela é uma empregada doméstica que deixou a filha quando criança para ir trabalhar e conseguir dinheiro para sustentar ela, isso resulta em anos sem ver o rosto da menina. E quero já falar a princípio que o ciclo estava prestes, vejam bem a palavra prestes pois não é uma confirmação do fato, a ser repetido. Quando descobrimos no final que Jessica havia viajado para São Paulo em busca de estudo para um futuro melhor, mas deixando o filho para trás. Essa é a realidade do nosso Brasil, mães solos que precisam ficar longe do filho para conseguir colocar comida na mesa, ciclos se repetindo porque "a minha mãe era empregada, e minha tia foi empregada, e minha avó era empregada, e minha bisavó também foi empregada.... E meus antepassados foram escravos". Um looping infinito. Isso pode ter sido quebrado no filme, porque afinal queremos filmes com finais felizes, para um final triste temos a realidade. Exatamente, a realidade, vai procurar por aí e irá encontrar milhares de mulheres como a Val que não tiveram um final feliz. Eu digo final feliz daquele momento que a Val pede demissão em diante, não sei se posso chamar de feliz toda a trajetória que ela precisou passar para finalmente estar perto da filha novamente. Podemos comentar brevemente o ponto sobre cuidar do filho de outra pessoa enquanto está longe do seu? A Val criou Fabinho a vida inteira de tal forma que ele preferia um abraço dela do que da própria mãe. E parecia uma eterna criança ao lado da Val, como o garotinho dela assim como quando era criança e ela estava lá por ele. Mas a realidade de Fábio ainda é uma realidade imensamente mais privilegiada, onde reprovar no vestibular o leva a um intercâmbio para Austrália. Porque o filho de rico vai tirar um tempo de férias, mas o filho de pobre tem que trabalhar pra pagar mais um ano de cursinho e torcer para passar na prova e entrar em uma faculdade com a esperança de quebrar o ciclo que a espera. Sabe aquela frase "Todo mundo tem um professor que te marcou", a Jéssica também teve um quando cita o ensino precário de onde estudou o ensino médio mas como um professor fez a diferença ao fazer eles pensarem de forma crítica e analisar as vias sociais em nosso mundo, a questionar, ter um pensamento próprio, uma opinião individual. É isso que faz a Jessica não se calar ao ver a forma como a mãe está sendo tratada a vida toda naquela casa onde trabalha, e ela mesma ao chegar na casa e em certo momento sendo referida até como "rato" por entrar na piscina. Porque para um bom entendedor meia palavra basta. Não quero nem citar aquele velho asqueroso com uma realidade criada em sua mente por uma fantasia com uma garota da mesma idade do seu filho. Devemos assistir mais nosso cinema nacional. Estamos perdendo muito e a oportunidade incrível de ver detalhes incrustados nessas obras que trazem tanto para nossa bagagem cultural, de conhecimento e vida.

texto: A pesar de que me pareció un poco aburrida, considero que hay diversos puntos interesantes en esta película: En primer lugar, como funcionan las dinámicas de poder. Para empezar, toda la relación de Val con su jefa y como a la dueña del hogar no le terminaba de caer bien Val. Se demostraba en cómo le hablaba, y más aún cuando llegó Jessica, ya que se mostraba menos sumisa a Val y la jefa parecía que pensaba que era inferior a ella. Un poco en relación a esto, también como los hombres piensan que tienen poder o derechos sobre una mujer por tener una "posición" y demás. Esto se demostraba con todo el tema de que Carlos se enamora de Jessica, hasta el punto de pedirle matrimonio, cuando ella nunca le dio indicios de que gustaba de él. Por otra parte, y un poco asociado a las relaciones de poder, se demuestra mucho la meritocracia. Val pensaba que ella no merecía ciertas cosas, como el helado, sentarse con sus jefes, estar en la piscina, y le intentaba instaurar este pensamiento a Jessica, pero ella no se dejaba. También, me pareció un poco interesante que Val se interesó en pasar más tiempo con Jessica cuando se dio cuenta que tenía un hijo. Lowkey lo asocié en que ella vio en el Jorge la oportunidad de cuidar y pasar tiempo con otro Fabinho. En general, siento que toca temas sociales bastante interesantes, sin embargo, la película me parecía un poco lenta y la trama/storytelling un poco aburrido.

texto: A pessoa já nasce sabendo, o que pode e o que não pode. Essa frase me marcou muito em Que Horas Ela Volta? , pois aqui é onde chegamos mais próximos do filme nos mostrar a raiz de todo o problema que a narrativa da obra nos sugere. Em outras palavras, por mais que saibamos que isso não é verdade, nos é imposto enquanto classe não dominante, desde que nascemos, que “naturalmente” temos um lugar definido na sociedade e que podemos até ascender, melhorar de vida, fazer “parte da família”, mas nunca estar no mesmo plano, mesmo lugar, mesma posição que a classe dominante, jamais. E é nesse contexto que trago o primeiro grande ponto positivo do filme: os enquadramentos. À Val, empregada da família, só lhe pertence um pequeno espaço, a cozinha, o quartinho pequeno e quente da empregada. Ela enxerga seus patrões através de uma parede que os divide, e portanto define muito bem o lugar de cada um. Ela só se junta a eles para servir e nada mais. No quarto dela, a câmera a filma atrás de uma grade, pois ela está presa e vulnerável dentro desse sistema. E o pior: por achar que é algo natural, que as coisas sempre foram assim, ela acaba acreditando que a vida dela é essa sem possibilidade de mudança. Ela cuida do filho dos patrões como se fosse seu, cuida da casa deles como se fosse sua, ela cuida de uma vida que não é dela e em troca deixa a própria vida e sua família de lado. Tudo isso por um valor financeiro baixo, injusto e explorado. É cruel. Mas aí entra o que seria o ponto-chave da virada: Jéssica, a filha de Val, vem para a cidade grande prestar vestibular e morar com a mãe (a quem mal consegue chamar de mãe, visto que Val teve que abdicar da própria família para ganhar a vida). Esse era para ser o grande motor de conscientização, mas, na minha visão, a personagem de Jéssica acaba sendo mal conduzida pelo roteiro. Não se trata apenas de uma rebeldia ou arrogância juvenil - o que seria compreensível, mas de uma falha no objetivo narrativo claro da personagem. Jéssica é pintada como extremamente inteligente, mas suas tentativas de conscientizar a mãe se resumem a gestos vazios, como dizer que ela pode entrar na piscina ou comer na mesa dos patrões, por exemplo. O que isso muda de fato no problema de classe? Na realidade material, se uma empregada doméstica decide usar a piscina dos patrões, ou ela sofre uma repreensão severa (afinal, eles detêm o poder financeiro e, por consequência, o poder sobre ela), ou é sumariamente demitida e substituída. Reduzir a emancipação de classe a esses "favores permitidos" esvazia a crítica. As falas e atitudes da Jéssica acabam soando rasas diante da grandiosidade do conflito que o próprio filme propõe. Obs: minha crítica quanto a isso é justamente a premissa narrativa política do filme, isso é esvaziado, raso, quase deixado de lado ao longo do filme. Ilustrando: A cena em que Bárbara, mãe da família, manda esvaziar a piscina depois que Jéssica entrou, falando que achou que tinha visto um rato ali é repugnante, é nojenta, dá raiva, mas isso no roteiro do filme não é explorado mais profundamente, não dá pra entender. Outra coisa que me incomodou: As cenas do pai da família com a Jéssica são muito constrangedoras também, até entendo o pensamento delas terem existido (hipocrisia e a objetificação velada da elite progressista…), mas mais uma vez cenas mal escritas e que no fim também ficaram sem sentido. O final também não me agrada, fica uma sensação de resolução simples que não resolve nada, afinal, se demitir do emprego explorador para finalmente viver mais de perto a sua própria vida junto de sua família, faz você de fato sair do sistema que anteriormente te fez abdicar de tudo isso? Não existe outra solução para ter uma vida mais digna junto das pessoas que você ama? Agora, o ponto alto do filme realmente é Val. Regina Casé brilhou aqui, personagem bem escrita demais, o filme é inteiramente dela. Fico de certa forma feliz de ter demorado um pouco pra ver esse filme, pois agora tive a oportunidade de assisti-lo com um olhar mais radicalizado politicamente. O capitalismo, como sempre a raiz do problema, dilacera famílias, criando um ciclo eterno de meninos e meninas perguntando “Que horas ela volta?” Um filme muito bom em expor o problema, mas pouco incisivo em mostrar a raiz, as soluções e uma conscientização mais crua dessa mesma questão. Ps: Adorei o fato de terem mostrado que o pai da família herdou tudo o que tem, ou seja, nos mostra que várias dessas famílias ricas e da elite herdaram seu patrimônio. Em outras palavras, essas pessoas não produzem nada, não trabalham, são vagabundas e vivem da exploração do trabalho alheio. 6,8/10

texto: É uma verdadeira aula de dissecação social que expõe a crueldade sutil e enraizada do classismo brasileiro com uma precisão cirúrgica. Que Horas Ela Volta? vai além de apontar o preconceito explícito. O filme escrutina a violência velada do paternalismo brasileiro (onde "ser tratado como da família" é apenas uma máscara polida para a servidão moderna), transformando o espaço doméstico em um campo de batalha psicológico. Tirando um debate cultural de longa data dos seus trilhos narrativos mais comuns, a obra consegue lançar uma luz crua e implacável sobre as microagressões diárias e os ciclos de desigualdade que atravessam gerações. A direção de fotografia é surpreendentemente brilhante, com enquadramentos deliberados e potentes que mapeiam visualmente os distanciamentos emocionais e as fronteiras sociais dentro de uma mesma casa. As escolhas audiovisuais acertam ao conseguir transformar um ambiente doméstico e silencioso em uma arena de conflito visualmente marcante e instigante. A todo momento, a narrativa desfere golpes discretos, mas ainda assim amargos, àqueles que compartilham da consciência de classe. O que mais me pegou, no entanto, foi uma compreensão silenciosa: Ouvir o menino perguntar "Que horas ela volta?" no início parece apenas um aceno inteligente ao título. Ouvir a mesmíssima pergunta vindo da própria filha da Val no final do filme me atingiu de forma elegante -- foi um susto junto à uma realização devastadora, tanto para o público quanto para a própria Val, nos lembrando do que foi sacrificado e por quem.

texto: Assistir o filme da visão do “patrão” é algo diferente. A princípio, percebe se como a vida inteira da val foi servir a família e como ela é totalmente dependente dos patrões, tanto por morar na residência na qual trabalha, tanto pelo apego emocional no jorginho. Ademais, o filme mostra a filha da val como a quebra da herança de servidão. Apesar da plena ingratidão em seus momentos com Val e de momentos invasivos para/ com a família, ela foi fundamental para libertar sua mãe, que posteriormente a libertou da herança de abandono, possibilitando a vinda de seu neto a são paulo. texto: FILMAÇO DA PORRA! esse é um dos melhores filmes que já assisti em toda a minha vida. o filme aborda delicadamente a realidade de muitas empregadas domésticas no brasil. a val é uma personagem cativante porque eu vi a minha mãe nela. assim como a personagem, minha mãe também trabalhou em casas de famílias ricas e cuidou dos filhos dos patrões. na verdade, a val nem parece uma personagem fictícia, ela foi representada com tanto cuidado e naturalidade que parecia alguém que eu conheço há anos. e isso vem da atuação absurda da regina casé. a chegada da jéssica na casa dos patrões representa uma ruptura nesse ciclo de submissão vivido pela mãe dela. jéssica não aceita as imposições de inferioridade, e o filme deixa muito evidente o desconforto da elite diante da ascensão social das classes populares e do acesso às universidades públicas. é doloroso pensar que a val dedicou a vida cuidando do fabinho enquanto mal pôde acompanhar o crescimento da própria filha. o filme faz tudo isso de maneira extremamente natural e realista. as atuações são tão boas que eu sentia cada silêncio desconfortável e todo o resto na pele. e puta que pariu, eu ODIEI a Bárbara e aquele marido escroto dela. o fabinho talvez seja o “melhorzinho” daquela família justamente por ter sido criado pela val e por realmente amar ela, mas ainda assim continua sendo um playboy que parece incapaz de fazer qualquer coisa sozinho, igual aos pais que não sabem levantar a bunda da cadeira pra colocar um simples prato na pia.

texto: aonde já se viu, filhos de empregados sentar na mesa dos patrões. sabe aquele filme que você assiste e se sente, ao mesmo tempo, acolhida, deslocada e desconfortável? eu vi muitos comentários no twitter de gente chamando jéssica de folgada, intrometida, sem noção e tudo mais. mas era muito compreensível que ela esperasse poder se sentir em casa naquele lugar. a mãe dela trabalhou a vida inteira naquela casa. val deixou de cuidar da própria filha pra cuidar do filho dos outros. e, de repente, quando a filha aparece e não aceita aquelas regras invisíveis de quem pode ou não pode ocupar determinados espaços, ela vira a errada. acho que essa parte me pega de um jeito mais pessoal também, porque eu já senti essa expectativa de pertencimento. e é muito interessante como o filme trabalha essa contradição em relação à val, porque os patrões dizem que ela é “como alguém da família”, que ela pertence àquela casa, mas isso só funciona enquanto essa proximidade não ameaça a hierarquia social daquele lugar. ela pode cuidar, limpar, cozinhar, criar o filho deles, conhecer a vida da família, estar presente em tudo… mas existem limites muito claros. ela pode ser “da família”, desde que determinados espaços, e isso incomoda profundamente aquela família. acho muito interessante porque muitas pessoas assistem ao comportamento dela justamente a partir da lógica daquela casa. e é muito louco perceber que até pessoas que já passaram por situações parecidas acabam reproduzindo essa lógica. a gente se acostuma tanto com determinados limites que começa a enxergá-los como naturais. e a atuação da regina casé é simplesmente foda. não sei nem que outra palavra usar. ela consegue fazer a val ser tão real que você entende a personagem mesmo quando ela toma atitudes que te incomodam. e o elenco inteiro é impecável, de verdade. é muito legal assistir esse filme também por causa disso. é um filme muito importante pra mim. fala sobre pertencimento, sobre classe social, sobre maternidade, sobre quem pode ou não pode ocupar determinados espaços e, principalmente, sobre como incomoda ver uma pessoa pobre ocupando um espaço que, socialmente, disseram a ela que não era dela. é um filme que sinceramente todo mundo deveria ver.

texto: Assistir o filme da visão do “patrão” é algo diferente. A princípio, percebe se como a vida inteira da val foi servir a família e como ela é totalmente dependente dos patrões, tanto por morar na residência na qual trabalha, tanto pelo apego emocional no jorginho. Ademais, o filme mostra a filha da val como a quebra da herança de servidão. Apesar da plena ingratidão em seus momentos com Val e de momentos invasivos para/ com a família, ela foi fundamental para libertar sua mãe, que posteriormente a libertou da herança de abandono, possibilitando a vinda de seu neto a são paulo. texto: An extreme movie that really goes all the way and beyond in terms of violence and gore which you seldomly see with a female filmmaker (Titane‘s extremity looks tame compared to this). But ironically, it has little substance and moves quickly off of its thin dramatic scaffolding into a nightmarish torture porn with a weak wink. It mixes any evil twin and body horror film you have ever seen into something memorably empty and removed. Watching this in Cannes with the audience reaction was a fun experience still.

texto: SFF2024 #7 (Closing Night Film) Spends a surprising amount of its third act riffing on extremely specific images from a not very well-regarded Doctor Who episode. This gets a lot of mileage out of its excellent concept, which allows for both lots of squeamishly fun body horror and plenty of (definitely unsubtle but undeniably worthwhile) social commentary about how we view women’s bodies culturally & the speed at which we tend to discard those on our screens once they reach a certain age. To her credit, Fargeat handles the topic deftly without resorting to the self-seriousness that trips up many a horror movie that sets out to say something about a specific issue, though I did feel at times that the film’s camp tone was keeping me at a slight ironic distance from the emotions of the characters. Said characters are brought to life nicely by the cast, though. I don’t think this is quite as much of a Demi Moore showcase as some of the Cannes critics hailed it as (by plot necessity, she’s off-screen for large chunks of the runtime), but it’s certainly bold, electric work from her. There’s a sequence where her character is overcome by body image-related insecurities while getting ready to go out, and it’s made as viscerally heartbreaking as it is by Moore’s excellent work. Margaret Qualley’s material is a bit more one-note but, as usual, she sells it on her screen presence alone (also, at the risk of proving the movie’s point, it must be said that she is quite hot). Dennis Quaid’s turn would be way too much in almost any other movie but it works for this one’s camp sledgehammer of an approach. Fargeat’s cooking with all the right ingredients here, but I think she undercuts herself with self-indulgence. There’s no real reason for this to be 140 minutes long; the concept could have easily made for a brilliant, punchy 90-minutes. By the third act, the movie just keeps piling hats onto hats in service of a gorefest that strays too far from the original allegory. It’s not that it isn’t a natural escalation of the conflict, per se, but I think it’s possible to escalate things a little too much, to the point where it becomes more numbing than impactful. There were several great possible endings in the climax, but Fargeat just kept dragging it out for no apparent reason, and the whole movie - while never boring - is similarly just a bit flabby given the simplicity of its plot. The film’s issues are not big enough to entirely sink it, but they definitely made me feel a bit out of step with the hype from Cannes. As recent Cannes-awarded, women-directed body horrors go, I’m much more of a Titane man.

texto: Un peu tiraillée pour le coup, il y a beaucoup de choses que j'ai aimé mais aussi beaucoup de points qui m'ont dérangé Dans le positif, j'applaudis le cast que j'ai trouvé parfait, j'aime la mise en scène (surtout dans la première partie), scène de fin très fun et certains plans que j'ai trouvé magiques (je retiens surtout ce plan sur Demi Moore, portant une robe dos nue, assise au bar) Dans le négatif maintenant : - J'ai trouvé le film un peu trop répétitif par moment, j'avais parfois l'impression que le film poussait des scènes de façon grossières par peur que le spectateur ne comprenne pas le message (mais tqt vraiment on comprend) - Troooop de scènes sur les fesses de Margarett, je t'adore mais ça ajoute de nouveau de la longeur inutile et un côté redondant et puis surtout ça vient presque contredire le message du film - C'est pas un film féministe et c'est bon ca commence à fatiguer de présenter tous les films réalisés par des femmes comme ça. C'est pas la faute de la réal bien sûr, mais le message pseudo féministe n'aide pas malheureusement... Compétition officielle

texto: SFF2024 #7 (Closing Night Film) Spends a surprising amount of its third act riffing on extremely specific images from a not very well-regarded Doctor Who episode. This gets a lot of mileage out of its excellent concept, which allows for both lots of squeamishly fun body horror and plenty of (definitely unsubtle but undeniably worthwhile) social commentary about how we view women’s bodies culturally & the speed at which we tend to discard those on our screens once they reach a certain age. To her credit, Fargeat handles the topic deftly without resorting to the self-seriousness that trips up many a horror movie that sets out to say something about a specific issue, though I did feel at times that the film’s camp tone was keeping me at a slight ironic distance from the emotions of the characters. Said characters are brought to life nicely by the cast, though. I don’t think this is quite as much of a Demi Moore showcase as some of the Cannes critics hailed it as (by plot necessity, she’s off-screen for large chunks of the runtime), but it’s certainly bold, electric work from her. There’s a sequence where her character is overcome by body image-related insecurities while getting ready to go out, and it’s made as viscerally heartbreaking as it is by Moore’s excellent work. Margaret Qualley’s material is a bit more one-note but, as usual, she sells it on her screen presence alone (also, at the risk of proving the movie’s point, it must be said that she is quite hot). Dennis Quaid’s turn would be way too much in almost any other movie but it works for this one’s camp sledgehammer of an approach. Fargeat’s cooking with all the right ingredients here, but I think she undercuts herself with self-indulgence. There’s no real reason for this to be 140 minutes long; the concept could have easily made for a brilliant, punchy 90-minutes. By the third act, the movie just keeps piling hats onto hats in service of a gorefest that strays too far from the original allegory. It’s not that it isn’t a natural escalation of the conflict, per se, but I think it’s possible to escalate things a little too much, to the point where it becomes more numbing than impactful. There were several great possible endings in the climax, but Fargeat just kept dragging it out for no apparent reason, and the whole movie - while never boring - is similarly just a bit flabby given the simplicity of its plot. The film’s issues are not big enough to entirely sink it, but they definitely made me feel a bit out of step with the hype from Cannes. As recent Cannes-awarded, women-directed body horrors go, I’m much more of a Titane man.

C'est pas la faute de la réal bien sûr, mais le message pseudo féministe n'aide pas malheureusement... Compétition officielle

texto: 5 stars for the cinematic experience that came with this movie. Without an audience I would have turned this off at the first transitioning scene. Filled with gore, horror, horniness and comedy The Substance was a lot - hence someone in the audience throwing up and fainting in the first 5 minutes of the film which should be taken as a compliment in this shocking genre. A great focus on existentialism and body dysmorphia for women all in hopes to please the embodiment of the rich touchy straight white male - the producer at a sexualised fitness TV program appropriately named Harvey (nice one). Many odes to other films such as The Shining and Trainspotting. Incredibly shot and well acted, I just don’t think this genre is for me. My jaw was on the floor and my ass cheeks were clenched, many sighs of relief when this came to an end.

texto: To put things briefly, The Substance is a relatively sound film, although, it still comes with a fair share of issues. As films of this more thematic nature, and more broadly within the horror genre typically demand, you’re sort of supposed to just go with the plot, which I struggle with. It’s not necessarily poorly written, it’s just contrived, not implausibly, but I still feel the beats could’ve been better strung together. Speaking of themes, it touches primarily on our contemporary culture, our media, and on the treatment of women, particularly within the public sphere; although I do find that the film fails to boldly challenge our perception of these social facets, or issues. For example, the premise, alongside how the film is shot evidently wish to discuss the self-objectification of the individual, of which is intrinsically tied to social norms, and to capitalism; yet this is highly surface level, and largely visual, it isn't actually protested. Overall, it's quite straightforward in its messaging, quite literally infantilising a woman, and I don’t have any qualms with it, however, a bit of nuance, or development upon these themes would’ve made the piece a touch more grounding, connecting, perhaps it might’ve helped alleviate the disconnect created by the grotesque body horror. On that, yeah, uhm, the film excels in disgusting me, although, I expected as much and genuinely struggled to convince myself to watch it. More technically, I was pleased in that colour wasn’t shied away from, as is the case frequently in this genre, and in this era; and the camerawork was solid, if albeit a bit uninspired—I also found it notable that some shots were clearly added solely for the sake of evoking disgust, or discomfort, even if the details were irrelevant, most prominently in the opening scenes of the film.

texto: La serie Z que rezuma. Sobre pinchazos y borbotones. Ya lo escribió Baruch Spinoza en su momento: nadie sabe lo que puede un cuerpo. Transcurrida una hora, me planteo si lo que estoy viendo es una película falsamente subversiva que parte de una idea explícita (la crítica a la sobreexposición del cuerpo femenino en la era del consumo, convertido en producto de carnicería a causa de la tiranía de la belleza) y la lleva al paroxismo. Sin embargo, conforme el relato avanza nos vamos encontrando con una suerte de retorno del espectro de "El hombre elefante", de "Carrie", de "Alien" y de otras múltiples tradiciones del cine norteamericano. Es contundente y celebratoria en el rumbo que toma y también divertida, e incluye una jocosa referencia a "Vertigo".

texto: This film is gonna be a huge divider. All I know is: I won't forget that screening in a hurry. Every Cannes has one: a love it or hate it title that becomes a word-of-mouth sensation thanks to the sheer division it creates among festivalgoers. No, we’re not talking about the so-bad-it-still-isn’t-good Megalopolis, but The Substance, a body horror that goes places even body horror aficionados will be shocked by. Helping this film’s cause are a few things – firstly, it’s the second film from Coralie Fargeat, whose gory thriller Revenge marked her out as one to watch back in 2017 – but, secondly it marks a return-of-sorts for 1990s icon Demi Moore, who is fantastically cast as an ageing Hollywood star who takes a black market drug to create a younger version of herself. The Substance is as gruesome as they come, culminating with an extended sequence that needs to be experienced with a crowd.

texto: Writing this review at midnight so… I tried following along with Pump It Up as I watched it and dislocated my leg, this is ridiculous, I want a refund. 0/10. A grotesquely made satire, that can be best described as equal parts gross, depressing, funny, and raunchy. Demi Moore and Margaret Qualley brought a lot to this, playing Elisabeth/Sue playing the dual identities to feel like the same person (after all they are one) but different enough to feel distinct. Dennis Quaid is great at playing the most disgusting part of the movie, Harvey. The real star of the show here is Fargeat’s directing. A visual and audial treat of a movie. Not a treat like candy but the talent on display is stunning and I hope she continues making more movies (I also caught a bit of Revenge but not enough for a review). Stunning use of color and not to mention the creature and body horror effects. A lot of the creature stuff didn’t really freak me out but Elisabeth/Sue’s body mangling and decaying had mc flinching. There’s a bit to be said on the films similarities to the manga Helter Skelter and Oliver Wilde’s The Picture of Dorian Grey. Which aren’t bad, nothing is original, and are distinct works but it’s interesting how they all handle the deterioration of self in search of beauty. How did Sue manage to build a small room in like, a few days. There’s a lot of heightened reality in this movie but that really took me out. I do think a few times the movie over explains its ideas, however that being said this is a thematically rich movie. The core is obvious, how women are treated within beauty standards, Elisabeth wants to maintain her youth and fame so she uses The Substance that’s the premise. The film shows that in a lot of ways how that’s enforced by men, Harvey’s introduction has him reference fertility ages, a note Elisabeth receives says “you WERE amazing, and when she interacts with the biker as Elisabeth and not as Sue, he yells at her. Harvey and the executives even say “pretty girls should always smile” before running off to chase dancers like dogs. Sue also enforces this. Giving Elisabeth an astronomically high standard, she cannot meet, although they are one. Both versions of Pump It Up are a good point here— Elisabeth’s show is mostly in a wideshot, instructions pretty clear. The leotard more of a cloth texture, though fitting, isn’t painted on. Then you have Sue’s… which is different. It’s a male gaze wet dream, a metallic bikini that’s practically spray painted on, is basically a thong on the bottom, and is cut to the point it can barely be considered athletic wear. It’s enforced on Elisabeth largely and more subtly on Sue. Funnily enough by the end, once everything goes wrong, that’s the only way the two could escape the cage of beauty standards. Two other threads I read in the film is within “respect the balance” is about self hatred and work life balance. Which going from male gaze to love yourself in theme is a leap but— Elisabeth and Sue hate eachother one considering her a “selfish bitch” the other an old woman who wastes her life. Yet they are the same person, they are one. Sue forces herself to work at Elisabteh’s expense, and Elisabeth does nothing in the meantime, just waiting for more Sue time. She buried herself in her career, and neglected any sort of relationships, that being familial, friendly, or otherwise. Her self-worth is her career, that’s all she has. And if she doesn’t have a career, she doesn’t have a self. Which she hates. While I just went on this whole thing about self hatred within the fact that though they are the same person Elisabeth and Sue hate eachother. I do think strangely enough, though it contradicts they have something that reads as a deeply messed up mother and daughter relationship. I think most of this comes from the interview scene. Elisabeth finds Sue spoiled, someone she gave life, someone who owes everything to her, and stealing away what she had. Sue thinks Elisabeth is jurassic, old, remarking she didn’t like the show but it was “inescapable”. Which does read a lot like a mother and daughters, not to so positive opinion of one another. It could be said that Elisabeth is exploiting the girl she created to extend her career, live through her, in this case literally. Though that does sort of ignore that Sue is defintley an extension of Elisabeth’s narcissism. Within that there’s two ways I see the Elisabeth/Sue fight. It’s either a manifestation of self hatred or a daughter trying to be her own person. Decide which one you like more, don’t debate in the comments. I do think the ending is far more campy than the first two hours but it’s not bad, a bloody wild climax. Anyways I’m glad to say The Substance has… The Substance in terms of theme and what it’s trying to say. Can’t wait to see whatever Fargeat does next, and though I’m not looking forward to it, I hope Demi Moore gets more work in the future, I’m sure Margaret Qualley will do great in the Posession remake.

texto: This film is gonna be a huge divider. All I know is: I won't forget that screening in a hurry. Every Cannes has one: a love it or hate it title that becomes a word-of-mouth sensation thanks to the sheer division it creates among festivalgoers. No, we’re not talking about the so-bad-it-still-isn’t-good Megalopolis, but The Substance, a body horror that goes places even body horror aficionados will be shocked by. Helping this film’s cause are a few things – firstly, it’s the second film from Coralie Fargeat, whose gory thriller Revenge marked her out as one to watch back in 2017 – but, secondly it marks a return-of-sorts for 1990s icon Demi Moore, who is fantastically cast as an ageing Hollywood star who takes a black market drug to create a younger version of herself. The Substance is as gruesome as they come, culminating with an extended sequence that needs to be experienced with a crowd.

texto: honestly loved how everything is shoved into your face via visual presentation and cues. some might criticize how this film exaggerates the message, slapping it on you with direct transparency as if it isn’t obvious enough, but in a world full of films buried in subtext, it’s refreshing to see one that makes the message painfully clear—especially since men (both as individuals and as a system) still don’t systematically grasp how physically, socially, and mentally detrimental beauty standards are for women. SO HELL YEAH, SHOVE THE MESSAGE UP THEIR ASSES. even the male looksmaxxing culture is just the tip of the iceberg compared to women's trenches. the dynamic between demi and margaret is excellent, and i cannot stress enough how good the casting is. demi’s performance evoked so much empathy in me, especially in her self‑destructive moments and when she tried to bring sue back, which eventually led to her gory death. elisa’s childhood friend really stood out to me, as he's such a symbolic figure or reminder of her potential recovery and self‑acceptance, though we all knew how their date would end. i definitely caught the significance of the final act, but it didn’t stand out because it felt comical. technically, everything is excellent, but again, monstra elisasue comes across as more comical than anything. i may or may not have missed the subtext if that was intentional. ultimately, all i can say is i fucking love depictions of female insecurities and frustrations with mirrors as cinematic tools.

texto: La madre de Dios. Creo que es la primera vez que estoy enfadado de verdad después de ver una película. He gastado 3 horas (¡¡¡3 HORAS!!!) en ver el musical más plano, insulso y procedural que podría imaginarme. - Todas las canciones son iguales, es que no puedes recordar ni una sola de ellas nada más terminarla. Le preguntas a ChatGPT como serían las canciones de un musical de Harry Potter en el mundo de las golosinas y te saca todo el repertorio. - La estética es todo lo contrario a lo que me gusta (aunque lo esperaba). Vestuario y decorado Broadway saturado. Te vomitan colorines sin parar y a otra cosa mariposa. - El tono infantil de Disney pero llevado al extremo ridículo. Es una película para niños, si, pero sin ninguna pretensión de segunda capa o mensaje que lo tienen casi todas aunque sea mínimo. Fuera coñas al nivel de una serie procedural slop de Nickelodeon en 2010. - El ritmo hace que parezca que llevas viendo días la película, infinito tiempo gastado en ABSOLUTA NADA. Te cuentan 5 fun facts del origen del Mago de Oz en un milenio. La he parado unas 15 veces. 3 horas para esto y todavía queda la segunda parte, es que no me lo creo. Y sí, la voy a ver, lo que me faltaba era quedarme a medias después de tragarme la mitad de este plato chino sabor glutamato refrito. Si en la tv interdimensional esa de Rick&Morty hicieran una parodia de la industria del cine actual saldría exactamente esto. Ver buenos musicales me quitó el prejuicio que tenía sobre ellos y es que esto es todo lo que yo pensaba que eran cuando tenía 15 años y era un edgy anime gore.

texto: Pretty solid! This was certainly more up my alley than I expected it to be. Everything is very maximalist here, to the point of being visually overwhelming at times. There was clearly a great amount of care and detail put into the set design. The dialogue was fun and I was a big fan of all the words they came up with in here. It's a fun twist on The Wizard of Oz, which I'm ashamed to say I only generally know the story of. I also only just found out that Wicked is not, in fact, an original screenplay and was adapted from a play. Apparently I live under a rock. There are certainly some gripes I have here, with the biggest one being the music. Composition felt very flat and just unmoving to me despite all of its attempts at grandness. Mixing was horrible, you can't hear any of the instruments over the vocals half the time. Vocal performances are reminiscent of how I feel about TOOL and Angine de Poitrine; there's a high level of technicality and little to no feeling. Music can be a make or break thing in a MUSICAL, but this seems to be mostly genre-based personal taste whatever so I won't be too harsh. I also thought it looked very visually fake a lot of the time. My girlfriend pointed out that a lot of the sets were actually real, and a surprising amount of the movie was done practically, which I found difficult to believe cause, well... look!! It just looks CGI as all hell!! But apparently it's true, there was a lot of work on the set designs here, and maybe it's that they did TOO good of a job that my brain fills in that it must be fake. Even then, so many shots have this sort of saccharinity to them that feels very common in these high-budget blockbusters where everything is filmed in a green room. Speaking of green... I felt like they didn't know how to deal with the main character being green. I wanted them to either REALLY lean into her sticking out visually or actually coordinate the shots so that the colors all go together (bonus points for all the nature-y segments that are super green and she's sort of like camouflaged almost I thought that was kind of funny) but most of the movie seemed to be in this sort of awkward middle ground between the two. Maybe it's supposed to say something about her lived experience or whatever but I didn't get that from it either. It suffers from the same problem a lot of blockbusters with A-list actors do, which is that they spend all this money on the background and hardly have the characters interact with it! Maybe it's some shallow depth of field so we can't even see anything, or maybe there's a bunch of cuts so that they can split a complicated shot into more manageable chunks, or any number of other things, but it never feels like we're actually supposed to explore the frame!! Everything happens in the middle, everything is immediately apparent what it means and where you're supposed to look and the subtext always finds a way to rise to the level of text and yada yada yada yada boring pretentious stuff YES I KNOW ITS A CHILDRENS MOVIE YES I HAD THE SAME COMPLAINTS WITH STAR WARS YES THE PROBLEM IS PROBABLY ME but still!! Like I go on and on about, can we please just stop with the medium close up over the shoulder dialogue shots!? I guess through all the rambling what I'm really trying to say is that so much of the technical side of things is done right. It's got the budget, the sweeping sets, all the lighting equipment you could ever ask for, super high quality cameras, and yet... it feels like they just stopped there. You got the cameras, now USE them!! In all the grandiosity of the sets, it feels like there wasn't much thought put into visual language. I think this could have been a better movie if the budget was cut by 90%, because it would have forced people to think and get creative about how to film stuff! I think the whole writing a blank check is detrimental because creativity so often is fostered by limitation. But even after saying all that, it is undeniable that this movie is very fun to just sit back and watch. It's almost 3 hours but doesn't even feel like 2. Cynthia Erivo and Ariana Grande have wonderful chemistry, the writing here is very entertaining, and if I turn off the pretentious side of my brain, it's very easy to get swept away by all of the visual sugar here. I am even excited to see the second part!!

texto: I struggle to call this a mixed bag because the good is not nearly as present in quantity as the bad. The film is a bit too comfortable with it's source material I think. It most consistently preforms when it is working as closely to the stage show as possible, i.e. the famously good music is still good. However it does not manage to overcome any of the flaws of the original product, nor I think, particularly thrill in it's limited ability to translate stage to film. Choreography and set design are both at best, adequate which is a shame for a product which should shine in both areas. Costuming is a bit better, but is kept down by the Netflix gray smudge color grading. How can you produce a film in Oz and not have any color! A world of bright shades is reduced to smudgy pinks, dull greens, and little else that is not seemingly grey or earth tone. The film is far worse for not having put in the work to be as delightful to look at as the original Oz film. The story is not very good, there is basically no modification from the stage show to my understanding, and the show has always coasted by on the musical numbers over the story. The same structure remains here, made worse by the fact this is only part one and several more hours of story remain. Overall a pretty unremarkable thing, it managed to never make me consider stopping watching, but not much beyond that in terms of impact.

texto: Pretty solid! This was certainly more up my alley than I expected it to be. Everything is very maximalist here, to the point of being visually overwhelming at times. There was clearly a great amount of care and detail put into the set design. The dialogue was fun and I was a big fan of all the words they came up with in here. It's a fun twist on The Wizard of Oz, which I'm ashamed to say I only generally know the story of. I also only just found out that Wicked is not, in fact, an original screenplay and was adapted from a play. Apparently I live under a rock. There are certainly some gripes I have here, with the biggest one being the music. Composition felt very flat and just unmoving to me despite all of its attempts at grandness. Mixing was horrible, you can't hear any of the instruments over the vocals half the time. Vocal performances are reminiscent of how I feel about TOOL and Angine de Poitrine; there's a high level of technicality and little to no feeling. Music can be a make or break thing in a MUSICAL, but this seems to be mostly genre-based personal taste whatever so I won't be too harsh. I also thought it looked very visually fake a lot of the time. My girlfriend pointed out that a lot of the sets were actually real, and a surprising amount of the movie was done practically, which I found difficult to believe cause, well... look!! It just looks CGI as all hell!! But apparently it's true, there was a lot of work on the set designs here, and maybe it's that they did TOO good of a job that my brain fills in that it must be fake. Even then, so many shots have this sort of saccharinity to them that feels very common in these high-budget blockbusters where everything is filmed in a green room. Speaking of green... I felt like they didn't know how to deal with the main character being green. I wanted them to either REALLY lean into her sticking out visually or actually coordinate the shots so that the colors all go together (bonus points for all the nature-y segments that are super green and she's sort of like camouflaged almost I thought that was kind of funny) but most of the movie seemed to be in this sort of awkward middle ground between the two. Maybe it's supposed to say something about her lived experience or whatever but I didn't get that from it either. It suffers from the same problem a lot of blockbusters with A-list actors do, which is that they spend all this money on the background and hardly have the characters interact with it! Maybe it's some shallow depth of field so we can't even see anything, or maybe there's a bunch of cuts so that they can split a complicated shot into more manageable chunks, or any number of other things, but it never feels like we're actually supposed to explore the frame!! Everything happens in the middle, everything is immediately apparent what it means and where you're supposed to look and the subtext always finds a way to rise to the level of text and yada yada yada yada boring pretentious stuff YES I KNOW ITS A CHILDRENS MOVIE YES I HAD THE SAME COMPLAINTS WITH STAR WARS YES THE PROBLEM IS PROBABLY ME but still!! Like I go on and on about, can we please just stop with the medium close up over the shoulder dialogue shots!? I guess through all the rambling what I'm really trying to say is that so much of the technical side of things is done right. It's got the budget, the sweeping sets, all the lighting equipment you could ever ask for, super high quality cameras, and yet... it feels like they just stopped there. You got the cameras, now USE them!! In all the grandiosity of the sets, it feels like there wasn't much thought put into visual language. I think this could have been a better movie if the budget was cut by 90%, because it would have forced people to think and get creative about how to film stuff! I think the whole writing a blank check is detrimental because creativity so often is fostered by limitation. But even after saying all that, it is undeniable that this movie is very fun to just sit back and watch. It's almost 3 hours but doesn't even feel like 2. Cynthia Erivo and Ariana Grande have wonderful chemistry, the writing here is very entertaining, and if I turn off the pretentious side of my brain, it's very easy to get swept away by all of the visual sugar here. I am even excited to see the second part!!

texto: Best moment: “Defying gravity”. That song and scene is the centerpiece of the musical and this (and the other) movie. It doesn’t disappoint. The song by itself already feels epic but the movie version puts a cherry on top. This small action interlude on the broom is a fun little break before it works toward that climax and note we have all been waiting for. Best quote: “I don’t cause commotions. I am one.” MVP: Cynthia Erivo. First, her voice is stunning. It is so crystal clear and she switches between emotional to powerful with the flip of vocal cord. Second, the acting matches the vocal performance. She gives Elphaba so much heart and a deep compassion but that fury beneath the surface is always brewing. It is an emotional performance in all areas. Best visual: The wizard’s room. The rest of the movie is so bright, colorful and joyful. That set, however, is darker and there isn’t any of the joy of the Emerald City. The design of the big head also looks really cool and ominous. Best showstopper: “Dancing through life” is just so much fun. The part in the library has so much cool choreography with the books and the spinning set. The ballroom looks stunning and also has some fun choreography. In all of this I ask myself one important question: How can someone be as charming as Jonathan Bailey? Rating: 9 out of 10 flying monkeys

texto: Der Film ist ja SO schnell over gewesen … Hat sich einfach wie ne Stunde angefühlt 🫪 Ja ich hab auch in drei Parts geguckt, aber die letzten 1,5 Stunden waren am Stück. Jede Szene ist cool und macht Spaß. Die Songs sind zum großen Großteil geil (auch wenn ich nicht ganz verstehe wie Defying Gravity der Hit aus dem Film geworden ist haha) und ich verstehe NULL wie das einfach kein Disney Film ist das ist ja einfach der krasseste non-Disney Disney-Film ever hahahaha Ich war echt lange bei vier Sternen, aber ich glaube ich gehe doch auf 3,5. Weil in dem Film passiert basically nichts. Es bringt die Story interessant und gut voran, aber die Plot-Punkte die gehittet werden sind einfach so kurz voneinander entfernt und wenige … Der 2,75-Stunden-Film hätte locker in nem schnell gepacten 20-Minuten-Kurzfilm passen können 💀💀💀 Vielleicht gehe ich aber auch wieder auf 4 … mal schauen, ich hab auf jeden Fall nen dollen Ohrwurm von Dancing through Life Hat trotzdem Spaß gemacht und ich hab sehr Bock auf Teil 2! Teil 1 endet ja sehr abrupt … Die komödiantischen Aspekte die ja eigentlich ausschließlich (?) von Ariana kommen sehr cool und mag-hasse ihren Character. Ich mochte auch die ganze Welt die erschaffen wurde SEHR. Zum Beispiel dass sie ständig Wörter überkorrigieren und dadurch falsch aussprechen. UND DIESEN KOPF VOM ZAUBERER WOW Ich finds bisschen komisch dass die Beziehung von Boq basically nur durch gaslighten entstand und auch immer noch solche Züge hat Und Junge haben die vergessen von log zu konvertieren 💀💀💀 (der Film sieht relativ grau aus) Ab der Emerald City sahs dann aber nice aus AH UND EDIT: Dafür dass ihre grüne Haut so ne große Rolle spielt ist die Begründung dafür SEHR schwach. I mean bisschen grünes trinken???????????

texto: Je n'avais pas la moindre envie de voir ce film avant aujourd'hui. J'en ressors pourtant ravie du détour. C'est pas le genre de film qui m'attire et pourtant c'est exactement ce dont j'avais envie. Un grand monde, une aventure, qui en fait des caisses mais qui raconte quand même. On me raconte des histoires simples et vieilles comme le monde et je les accueille avec un regard d'enfant. Voilà ce que je cherchais en fait, un film que j'aurais pu regarder dans le canap quand j'étais petite. Ce voyage là. Celui qui demande pas grand chose de plus que de se laisser faire. Celui qui me divertit pour me remonter le moral. Ça va mieux maintenant, cool !

texto: M(a)y Korea Challenge 2025 38. SK Drama A completely superfluous remake of The Housemaid which is worse in every way. The maid gets a new backstory and Youn Yuh-jung, in her debut role, plays her as if "girl from the country" was a mental disorder. Less of a threatening sexual force she is just another broken trauma doll, infantile and ready to be abused. Overall, the menacing presence of female agency is replaced by brute masculine force (read: rape scenes, endowed with a giallo -esque visual flair). The "cautionary tale" framing narrative of the previous version, with its charmingly bizarre final scene, is traded for a clichéed police investigation. And since the children play no role at all, and simply disappear after a few early scenes, I even miss Ahn Sung-Ki's bratty antics. Nah; this was an unnecessary disappointment.

texto: This is hardly a femme fatale story. More like a tale of extreme marital dysfunction and some lost soul that gets twisted up in it. The phrase ‘country girl’ seems to be used as a euphemism for prostitute or someone lesser. Myeong-ja spends the whole time trying to find increasingly extreme ways of responding to trauma, leading to disaster not entirely of her own making. I also didn’t quite get the commentary in the beginning regarding the aggressive youth in the post-Cold War environment, referring to the crazed teenagers unrelated to the household crime. The scene didn’t quite translate to the main character story at all but seemed to be given a particular weight regardless.

texto: Myeong-ja convinced me to drink rat poison. I haven't seen The Housemaid by the same director and I think that's a bit of a problem as this is a heavily stylised and hysterically acted variation on the film he laid down over a decade earlier. Everything here has a melodrama turned up to the highest settings and the cast's performances become so flailing and ridiculous that you wonder if the film is insisting on not being taken seriously. What's more most of the cool stylisation is really front loaded and that's before the dialogue completely goes to crazy town so you're left with a first half that routinely looks really interesting and a tone which is off-kilter but not completely lost and then a second half where people are just having wild emotional swings and routinely falling in to complete hysteria in sets you've now seen a dozen times with lighting that can only be described as generic. The final sequence with two of the characters still manipulating future events whilst dying from having ingested rat poison did win me back a bit though. I'm still sat here having no clue what the film was even trying to do which makes critiquing it quite hard. Freya's rating: 1/5

texto: I do love a good love triangle in Korean cinema, it always promises to be a good, but bonkers, time. This movie doesn’t take long to start going off the rails and it stays off the rails in some impressive ways throughout the rest of the movie. The acing is over the top but it matches the aggressive use of color and camera work that dominate the aesthetic style of this movie. I do think that the movie is probably a little bit too fast paced (there isn’t enough exposition at times), but it’s hard to keep your eyes off of what is happening on screens and all of the elements are working well together.

texto: “Director Kim Ki-young returns to continue his Housemaid trilogy with Woman of Fire and does it with an entertaining story, cast, and unsureness.” 10 years after The Housemaid, the director returns, and to provide an entry in his trilogy, Woman Of Fire is the second film with similar themes as The Housemaid, in fact, the story and character motivations are pretty similar as well. Once again the characters are fun and interesting especially the maid. The acting isn’t on the level of the previous film however it's not bad either. The story follows Dongsik and his family being thrown into turmoil when a new housemaid joins. The decade gives filmmakers the option for colored photography rather than going black and white which helped the first film a lot. The color is amazing, it's dulled and contrasted though however, it's nice to color costumes, props, and backgrounds. The thriller aspects of the film are pretty mundane and regular. IF you have seen any thriller film you know what is going to happen and if like me, you saw the first film then you pretty much know the whole film from the start to finish. Overall, a short and side-tracking film that you can watch when feeling adventurous with your watchlist.

texto: I have to respect a director who does a remake of a film he himself made only about a decade prior, but takes it in such a stylistically different direction. Personally, I preferred The Housemaid, but that doesn't take anything away from what was accomplished here; there seemed to be far less empathizing with the patriarch and far more agency lended to his wife, as well as a considerable amount of vibrant, sorta psychedelic use of color. It's nothing totally new, yet nothing too redundant.

texto: I heard this movie's is in similar territory to Ki-young Kim's more well-known 1960 shocker The Housemaid, but I didn't know it's gonna be a virtual remake. The movie tells a very similar story, almost beat to beat, with all the same strengths and weaknesses of the earlier version. Only this time it's in color, in widescreen, and with a markedly different ending.

texto: First remake of the original film The Housemaid by the same director a decade later.  This one has a similar cadence but the garish color palette is vastly different from the original black and white.  The menace of the mistress happens sooner and more obviously in this version. The seduction of the husband has a very similar feeling of inevitability, as if everyone is powerless to stop it. texto: “Director Kim Ki-young returns to continue his Housemaid trilogy with Woman of Fire and does it with an entertaining story, cast, and unsureness.” 10 years after The Housemaid, the director returns, and to provide an entry in his trilogy, Woman Of Fire is the second film with similar themes as The Housemaid, in fact, the story and character motivations are pretty similar as well. The story follows Dongsik and his family being thrown into turmoil when a new housemaid joins. The decade gives filmmakers the option for colored photography rather than going black and white which helped the first film a lot. The color is amazing, it's dulled and contrasted though however, it's nice to color costumes, props, and backgrounds. The thriller aspects of the film are pretty mundane and regular. IF you have seen any thriller film you know what is going to happen and if like me, you saw the first film then you pretty much know the whole film from the start to finish. Overall, a short and side-tracking film that you can watch when feeling adventurous with your watchlist.

texto: I discovered by watching this that Woman of Fire that it's essentially a remake of The Housemaid , the last movie I watched. It's really strange that despite the controversy surrounding The Housemaid that they would remake it only ten years later. It's even stranger that after several wars and censorship implementations this would be one of the few surviving films left in Korean cinema. It's about 85 percent the same but it starts and ends differently. Our two female leads have a different and darker beginning from their counterparts in The Housemaid and there are a few different deaths along the way. In general I didn't like Woman of Fire as much. texto: A remake/retelling of Kim's own film, The Housemaid (1960). Whereas the earlier movie addresses the concerns of creeping materialism into Korean society in the aftermath of the war, Woman of Fire uses the same narrative to plot a more sexually-charged tale focusing on the exploitation and subjugation of women in a highly conservative and patriarchal society. Woman of Fire is a gripping and evocative story which focuses on bodily autonomy, inter-relation power dynamics and violence towards women which, sadly, still feels rather topical even whilst watching this in 2020. Mixing elements of horror and melodrama, this is a highly engaging movie which (alongside Kim's other films) have had a clear and deep impact on modern Korean cinema - watching this, we can see the direct influence it had on Bong Joon-ho's Parasite. It is a deep shame that Kim Ki-yong's films have yet to find themselves included in the established canon of popular world cinema but, with Parasite providing a belated breakthrough for Korean cinema onto the world stage, belated recognition for one of the most unique voices in movie history is a distinct possibility.

texto: Woman of Fire , the second film in Kim Ki-Young’s “Housemaid Trilogy," is an interesting variation on Kim’s exceptional classic The Housemaid that's dominated by explosive colors (red and blue especially), aggressive camerawork, sexual acts obscured and spliced with suggestive photomontages thanks to censorship, and over-the-top acting. Similar to the original, this remake centers a love triangle (or "eternal triangle") between a middle class married couple and a housemaid, who is a country bumpkin this time around. Having now seen this, I'm of the belief that, in addition to the original, it also influenced 2010's The Housemaid . I appreciate the focus on class and gender dynamics as well as the central theme of "contamination" as the protagonists become corrupted and steadily deviate from their moral values as the narrative unfurls. I also like the reoccurring use of the need/desperation for water, which can be interpreted as a metaphor for a desire for "purification." This film trades in nuance and narrative substance for being exaggerated, absurd, and stylish - this isn't necessarily a bad thing, I'm just stating a fact; it works for what Kim is trying to accomplish. It's also more "seedy" and depraved than the original, but not in a way that makes it better or worse than the original - I just see it as another more modernized, differentiating aspect of this reimagining of the lurid housemaid tale. While not on par with the original (IMO), Woman of Fire is certainly a spicy, twisted, and entertaining psychosexual melodrama. 🌟 Why I Love East Asian Cinema 🌟

texto: "You can learn a lot by watching how rich people live." I kind of don't know what to make of this film, wickedly entertaining as it is. Myeong-Ja is obviously the product of repeated sexual violence and everything she does in the aftermath, I kind of stand by. She kind of exists within the tradition of monstrous women who transform into vengeful entities intent on destroying men, your Gumihos, Deer Women, Sirens, etc. The woman who buys her, Jeong-Suk says that she is a ghost haunting their home and it isn't untrue. Myeong-Ja was a young girl forced to perform menial labor, starved and left for dead after having her pregnancy forcefully terminated without her consent. There are no innocent victims. In the end, she assumes the role of predator and reverses the dynamic she was thrust in. As such, I don't entirely buy that the filmmakers set out to say that the unpaid housemaid is herself evil, albeit more than a bit mischievous. She is just inevitable. By the end, she ends up controlling that house and for the most part gets exactly what she wants. I would dare to say the biggest upset of this film is Jeong-Suk saying about the man who impregnated another woman in her own home, "He was always a good husband to me." Diva, you punished this girl but forgave your shitty husband multiple times. Can't even feel bad for you, you should've left his ass! But then we'd also have to talk about why women stay in relation to horrible men and that would be too much of a bummer.

texto: 🇰🇷March is Korea Month🇰🇵 One of those curious instances where a director remade his own previous film. In this case, Kim Ki-young redoes his seminal potboiler “ The Housemaid ” in color with a few minor plot tweaks and a bit more experimental editing. We see more of the housemaid’s perspective this time, where her actions are informed by a traumatic past while living in the country. She and a friend move to the city to start fresh only for her to get romantically involved with the husband of the family she serves. Youn Yuh-jung delivers an off kilter performance that occasionally comes across like camp, where she seems to be trying too hard to play crazy. The color is noticeable enough to seemingly justify the remake from a visual perspective, but I kept pining for the starkness of the original’s black and white. Overall I just preferred the original, especially since this broadly just felt like the same movie again, but it hits the beats needed to tell the story decently. A warning for those interested, the version that’s streaming on Tubi has a weird blurring at the bottom of the screen during every line of dialogue, and the whole image is noticeably cropped. I have to assume this print originally had burned in subtitles, and someone did some digital work to try and remove them. Also the subtitles that were provided are humorous in their descriptive quality. Early on there’s a flashback, and it’s accompanied by the subtitle “she remembers her past.” Three and a half stars.

texto: A distinct enough remake of the original The Housemaid with amped up moral decline and some very interesting camerawork. The psychedelic imagery didn’t really do it for me personally, but was a unique touch. The altered story felt less real but allows Myeong-Ja to develop into an arguably more compelling femme fatale. Overall, I prefer the original, but this one is still enjoyable.

texto: Going into this, I hadn't realized this is was supposed to be a remake in essence of Kim Ki-young's own seminal film The Housemaid from a decade prior. I also didn't know this was Youn Yuh-jung's first film, and she is an absolute scene stealer in this. There were some aspects of this I appreciated more than The Housemaid such as the camerawork and certain audio moments. The ending became a little overly dramatic and unnecessary complicated for my taste, but still a worthwhile watch.
